title.zh: 卷八十一 志第三十四 律曆十四
title.raw: 卷八十一 志第三十四 律曆十四 Volume 81 Treatises 34: Measures and Calendar 14

sentences.zh: 中原既失，禮樂淪亡。

translations.literal: With the Central Plains already lost, rites and music fell into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Central Plains were lost, the rites and music of the dynasty were lost as well.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，胡銓著《審律論》，曰：

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Gaozong, Hu Quan wrote the Treatise on Examining Pitch Standards, saying:
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Gaozong, Hu Quan composed the Treatise on Examining Pitch Standards, in which he wrote:

sentences.zh: 臣聞司馬遷有言曰：「六律為萬事根本，其于兵械尤所重，望敵知吉凶，聞聲效勝負，百王不易之道也。」

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Sima Qian said: "The six pitch standards are the root of the ten thousand affairs; in military weapons they are especially valued—gazing at the enemy one knows fortune and misfortune, hearing sounds one imitates victory and defeat; this is the way of the hundred kings that does not change."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard Sima Qian say: "The six pitch pipes are the foundation of all things; in warfare and weaponry they are especially important—by observing the enemy one can discern good and ill fortune, and by hearing sounds one can tell victory from defeat. This is the unchanging principle of the hundred kings."

sentences.zh: 臣嘗深愛遷之言律於兵械為尤重，而深惜後之談兵者止以戰鬥、擊刺、奇謀，此律之所以汨陳而學者未嘗道也。

translations.literal: Your servant has deeply admired Qian's words that pitch standards are especially important in military weapons, yet deeply regretted that later discussants of warfare speak only of battle, thrusting, and stratagems—this is why pitch standards have been muddied in presentation and scholars have never discussed them.
translations.idiomatic: I have long admired Qian's insistence that pitch standards matter most of all in military affairs, yet I deeply regret that later military theorists speak only of combat, thrusting, and clever stratagems. That is why pitch standards have been obscured in the literature and scholars have scarcely discussed them.

sentences.zh: 夫律、度、量、衡，古也淵源于馬遷，濫觴于班固，劉昭挹其流，孟康、京房、錢樂之之徒汨其泥而揚其波。

translations.literal: As for pitch standards, measures, quantities, and balances—the ancients traced their deep source to Sima Qian, their first trickle to Ban Gu; Liu Zhao drew up their current, while Meng Kang, Jing Fang, Qian Yuezhi, and the like muddied their silt and raised their waves.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch standards, measures, quantities, and balances: the ancients traced their deepest source to Sima Qian and their first stream to Ban Gu; Liu Zhao drew from their current, while Meng Kang, Jing Fang, Qian Yuezhi, and others stirred the mud and sent the waves higher.

sentences.zh: 遷之言曰：「黃鐘之實八十一以為宮，而以九為法，實如法，得長一寸，則黃鐘為九寸矣。

translations.literal: Qian's words say: "The volume of Yellow Bell is eighty-one to serve as the palace tone; taking nine as the divisor, when the volume accords with the divisor one obtains a length of one inch—then Yellow Bell is nine inches.
translations.idiomatic: Qian writes: "The volumetric standard of Yellow Bell is eighty-one, which serves as the foundation tone; with nine as the divisor, when volume and divisor are in proportion one obtains a length of one inch—thus Yellow Bell measures nine inches.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之實十七萬七千一百四十七，而以一萬九千六百八十三為法，實如法，亦得長一寸，亦黃鐘為九寸也。

translations.literal: The volume of Yellow Bell is one hundred seventy-seven thousand one hundred forty-seven, while nineteen thousand six hundred eighty-three serves as the divisor; when volume accords with the divisor one likewise obtains a length of one inch—Yellow Bell is likewise nine inches.
translations.idiomatic: The volumetric standard of Yellow Bell is 177,147, with 19,683 as the divisor; when volume and divisor are in proportion one still obtains a length of one inch—Yellow Bell is still nine inches.

sentences.zh: 然則十七萬七千一百四十七與夫所謂八十一者，雖多少之不同，而其實一也；

translations.literal: Thus one hundred seventy-seven thousand one hundred forty-seven and what is called eighty-one, though different in magnitude, are one in substance;
translations.idiomatic: Thus 177,147 and the figure called eighty-one differ in magnitude, yet their substance is one and the same;

sentences.zh: 萬九千六百八十三與夫所謂九者，雖多少之不同，而其法一也。

translations.literal: nineteen thousand six hundred eighty-three and what is called nine, though different in magnitude, are one in method.
translations.idiomatic: and 19,683 and the figure called nine differ in magnitude, yet their method is one and the same.

sentences.zh: 又曰，丑二，寅八，卯十六，辰六十四。

translations.literal: He also said: Chou two, Yin eight, Mao sixteen, Chen sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He also states: for Chou, two; for Yin, eight; for Mao, sixteen; for Chen, sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 夫丑與卯，陰律也；

translations.literal: Now Chou and Mao are yin pitch standards;
translations.idiomatic: Chou and Mao are yin pitch pipes;

sentences.zh: 寅與辰，陽律也。

translations.literal: Yin and Chen are yang pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Chen are yang pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 生陰律者皆二，所謂下生者倍其實；

translations.literal: Those that generate yin pitch standards are all two—what is called lower generation doubles the volume;
translations.idiomatic: Those that generate yin pipes all use two—what is called "lower generation" doubles the volumetric standard;

sentences.zh: 生陽律者皆四，所謂上生者四其實。

translations.literal: those that generate yang pitch standards are all four—what is called upper generation quadruples the volume.
translations.idiomatic: Those that generate yang pipes all use four—what is called "upper generation" quadruples the volumetric standard.

sentences.zh: 遷之言財數百，可謂簡矣，而後之言律者祖焉，是不亦淵源于馬遷乎？

translations.literal: Qian's words on pitch standards number several hundred and may be called concise; yet later speakers on pitch standards take him as ancestor—is this not also tracing the deep source to Sima Qian?
translations.idiomatic: Qian's remarks on pitch standards run to several hundred words and are remarkably concise, yet later theorists of pitch all treat him as their founder—does this not show that the deepest source lies with Sima Qian?

sentences.zh: 固之言曰：黃鐘之實，八百一十分。

translations.literal: Gu's words say: The volume of Yellow Bell is eight hundred ten parts.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu states: The volumetric standard of Yellow Bell is 810 parts.

sentences.zh: 蓋遷意也。

translations.literal: This is essentially Qian's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: This follows Sima Qian's intent.

sentences.zh: 然以林鐘之實五百四十，而乃以為六百四十，林鐘、太蔟之實以其長自乘，則聲雖有，小同于黃鐘之宮耳。

translations.literal: Yet taking the volume of Forest Bell as five hundred forty, he nevertheless treats it as six hundred forty; the volumes of Forest Bell and Great Cluster, multiplied by their own lengths, yield tones that exist but differ only slightly from the palace tone of Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he gives the volumetric standard of Forest Bell as 540 but treats it as 640; when the standards of Forest Bell and Great Cluster are multiplied by their respective lengths, tones are produced, but they differ only slightly from the Yellow Bell foundation tone.

sentences.zh: 然則魏柴玉制律，而與黃鐘商、徵不合，其失兆此矣。

translations.literal: Thus when Wei Chaiyu made pitch standards, they did not accord with the commercial and fifth tones of Yellow Bell—the omen of his error lay here.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Chai Yu of Wei fashioned pitch pipes, they failed to match the commercial and fifth tones derived from Yellow Bell—the root of his error lay here.

sentences.zh: 夫自子一分，終於亥十七萬七千一百四十七分，蓋遷術也。

translations.literal: From one part at Zi, ending at Hai with one hundred seventy-seven thousand one hundred forty-seven parts—this is Qian's method.
translations.idiomatic: From one part at Zi to 177,147 parts at Hai—this is Sima Qian's computational method.

sentences.zh: 而固亦曰，太極元氣，函三為一，始動於子，參之於丑，歷十二辰之數，而得黃鐘之實，以為陰陽合德，化生萬物。

translations.literal: Gu also says: The primordial vital breath of the Supreme Ultimate, enclosing three as one, first stirs at Zi, is tripled at Chou, passes through the numbers of the twelve branches, and thereby obtains the volume of Yellow Bell, taking this as the union of yin and yang virtues to generate and transform the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu likewise writes that the primordial qi of the Supreme Ultimate, containing three within one, first stirs at Zi, is tripled at Chou, passes through the twelve earthly branches, and thereby yields the volumetric standard of Yellow Bell—by which yin and yang unite in virtue to generate the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 其說蓋有本矣。

translations.literal: His theory indeed has a foundation.
translations.idiomatic: His theory does have a foundation.

sentences.zh: 然其言三分蕤賓損一，下生大呂，而不言夫所謂濁倍之變何？

translations.literal: Yet he speaks of the three-part Flaring Guest diminished by one to lower-generate Great Clarity, without explaining what is called the muddy doubled transformation—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he describes diminishing Flaring Guest by one-third to lower-generate Great Clarity, without explaining what is meant by the muddy doubled variant—why?

sentences.zh: 夫蕤賓之比于大呂，則蕤賓清而大呂濁，今又損二分之一以生大呂，則大呂之聲乃清於蕤賓，是不知夫倍大呂之濁。

translations.literal: As for Flaring Guest compared with Great Clarity, Flaring Guest is clear and Great Clarity muddy; now diminishing by one-half again to generate Great Clarity, Great Clarity's tone would be clearer than Flaring Guest's—this shows ignorance of doubling Great Clarity's muddiness.
translations.idiomatic: Relative to Great Clarity, Flaring Guest is the higher tone and Great Clarity the lower; yet if one diminishes by half again to generate Great Clarity, Great Clarity would sound higher than Flaring Guest—this shows ignorance of the muddy doubled form of Great Clarity.

sentences.zh: 然則蕭衍之論，至於夾鐘而裁長三寸七分，其失兆此矣。

translations.literal: Thus in Xiao Yan's theory, reaching Pinched Bell he trimmed the length to three inches seven parts—the omen of his error lay here.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in Xiao Yan's theory, when he reached Pinched Bell he cut the length to three inches and seven-tenths—the root of his error lay here.

sentences.zh: 是不亦濫觴于班固乎？

translations.literal: Is this not also the first trickle from Ban Gu?
translations.idiomatic: Does this not also trace its first stream to Ban Gu?

sentences.zh: 昭之言曰：推林鐘之實至十一萬八千九十八、太蔟之實至十五萬七千四百六十四，二乘而三約之者，為下生之實；

translations.literal: Zhao's words say: Extending the volume of Forest Bell to one hundred eighteen thousand ninety-eight and Great Cluster to one hundred fifty-seven thousand four hundred sixty-four—what is multiplied by two and reduced by three becomes the volume for lower generation;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao writes: Projecting the volumetric standard of Forest Bell to 118,098 and of Great Cluster to 157,464—what is multiplied by two and reduced by three yields the standard for lower generation;

sentences.zh: 四乘而三約之者，為上生之實。

translations.literal: what is multiplied by four and reduced by three becomes the volume for upper generation.
translations.idiomatic: what is multiplied by four and reduced by three yields the standard for upper generation.

sentences.zh: 此遷、固之意，昭則詳矣。

translations.literal: This is the meaning of Qian and Gu; Zhao made it detailed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the intent of Sima Qian and Ban Gu; Liu Zhao elaborated it in full.

sentences.zh: 然以蕤賓為上生大呂，而大呂乃下生夷則，何也？

translations.literal: Yet taking Flaring Guest to upper-generate Great Clarity, while Great Clarity lower-generates Leveling Tone—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he has Flaring Guest upper-generate Great Clarity, while Great Clarity lower-generates Leveling Tone—how can this be?

sentences.zh: 蓋昭之說陽生陰為下生，陰生陽為上生。

translations.literal: Zhao's theory holds that yang generating yin is lower generation, yin generating yang is upper generation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao's theory holds that when yang generates yin it is lower generation, and when yin generates yang it is upper generation.

sentences.zh: 今以蕤賓為上生大呂，則是陽生陰，乃上生也；

translations.literal: Now taking Flaring Guest to upper-generate Great Clarity, yang generating yin is nevertheless upper generation;
translations.idiomatic: Now if Flaring Guest upper-generates Great Clarity, yang generating yin is treated as upper generation;

sentences.zh: 以大呂為下生夷則，是陰生陽，乃下生也。

translations.literal: taking Great Clarity to lower-generate Leveling Tone, yin generating yang is nevertheless lower generation.
translations.idiomatic: and if Great Clarity lower-generates Leveling Tone, yin generating yang is treated as lower generation.

sentences.zh: 其蔽亦由不知夫大呂有濁倍之變，則其視遷、固去本遠矣。

translations.literal: His obscuration also stems from not knowing that Great Clarity has the muddy doubled transformation—thus his view of Qian and Gu departs far from the root.
translations.idiomatic: His error likewise stems from ignorance of Great Clarity's muddy doubled variant—thus his reading of Sima Qian and Ban Gu strays far from the root.

sentences.zh: 是不亦挹其流于劉昭乎？

translations.literal: Is this not also drawing up their current from Liu Zhao?
translations.idiomatic: Does this not also show him drawing from Liu Zhao's current?

sentences.zh: 若夫孟康、京房、錢樂之之徒，則又大不然矣。

translations.literal: As for Meng Kang, Jing Fang, Qian Yuezhi, and the like, they are again greatly at odds.
translations.idiomatic: As for Meng Kang, Jing Fang, Qian Yuezhi, and their followers, they were even further astray.

sentences.zh: 夫班固以八十一分為黃鐘之實，起十二律之周徑，度其長以容其實，初末嘗有徑三圍九之說也。

translations.literal: Ban Gu took eighty-one parts as the volume of Yellow Bell, established the circumference and diameter of the twelve pitch standards, measured their length to contain their volume—from first to last he never had the theory of diameter three circumference nine.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu took eighty-one parts as the volumetric standard of Yellow Bell, derived the circumference and diameter of the twelve pitch pipes, and measured their length to contain their volume—he never advanced the theory of "diameter three, circumference nine."

sentences.zh: 康之徒惑於八十一分之實，以一寸為九十分，而不察方圜之異，於是有徑三圍九之論興焉。

translations.literal: Kang and his followers, confused by the eighty-one-part volume, took one inch as ninety parts without discerning the difference between square and round—thus the theory of diameter three circumference nine arose.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Kang and his followers, misled by the eighty-one-part standard, treated one inch as ninety parts without noticing the difference between square and circular measures—thus the "diameter three, circumference nine" theory arose.

sentences.zh: 天律之形圜，如以為徑三圍九，則刓其四用之方，而不足於九分之數，以之容黍，豈能至於千二百哉！

translations.literal: Heavenly pitch standards are round in form; if one takes diameter three circumference nine, one trims away the square of its four usable sides and falls short of the ninety-part count—using it to contain millet, how could it reach one thousand two hundred!
translations.idiomatic: The pitch pipes of heaven are circular; if one applies "diameter three, circumference nine," one cuts away the square usable on four sides and falls short of the ninety-part measure—how could such a vessel hold 1,200 grains of millet!

sentences.zh: 然則所謂圍九，方分也。

translations.literal: Thus what is called circumference nine is square parts.
translations.idiomatic: Thus what is called "circumference nine" refers to square parts.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: How does one know this?
translations.idiomatic: How do we know this?

sentences.zh: 知龠之方，則知黃鐘之分亦方也。

translations.literal: Knowing that the yue is square, one knows that the parts of Yellow Bell are also square.
translations.idiomatic: Once one knows the yue measure is square, one knows the fractional parts of Yellow Bell must be square as well.

sentences.zh: 固雖無明說，其論洛下閎起曆之法曰：「律容一龠，積八十一寸，則一日之分也。」

translations.literal: Though Gu has no explicit statement, his discussion of Luoxia Hong's method for establishing the calendar says: "The pitch standard contains one yue; accumulated eighty-one inches make one day's fraction."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu offers no explicit statement, but in discussing Luoxia Hong's method for establishing the calendar he writes: "The pitch pipe holds one yue; accumulated to eighty-one inches, this yields one day's fractional measure."

sentences.zh: 夫八十一寸者，是乃八百一十分，以千二百黍納之龠中，則不搖而自滿，是無異黃鐘之容也。

translations.literal: Eighty-one inches are in fact eight hundred ten parts; placing one thousand two hundred grains of millet in the yue, it fills without shaking—this is no different from the capacity of Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty-one inches are in fact 810 parts; when 1,200 grains of millet are placed in the yue, it fills without shaking—no different from the capacity of Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 龠之制，方寸而深八分。

translations.literal: The yue is made one inch square and eight-tenths deep.
translations.idiomatic: The yue is one inch square and eight-tenths of an inch deep.

sentences.zh: 一龠之方，則黃鐘之分，安得而不方哉！

translations.literal: If one yue is square, how could the parts of Yellow Bell fail to be square!
translations.idiomatic: If a single yue is square, how could the fractional parts of Yellow Bell be anything but square!

sentences.zh: 圍九方分而圜之，則徑不止於三分矣。

translations.literal: Circumference nine as square parts made round—the diameter would be more than three parts.
translations.idiomatic: If "circumference nine" square parts were made circular, the diameter would exceed three parts.

sentences.zh: 故夫徑三圍九之說，孟康為之也。

translations.literal: Thus the theory of diameter three circumference nine was made by Meng Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the "diameter three, circumference nine" theory was Meng Kang's invention.

sentences.zh: 然由律生呂，數十有二，止矣；

translations.literal: Yet from pitch standards are generated the pitch pipes—twelve in number, and there it stops;
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the pitch standards the twelve pitch pipes are generated, and there the count stops;

sentences.zh: 京氏演為六十，錢樂之廣為三百六十，則與黃帝之說悖矣。

translations.literal: Jing's school expanded them to sixty, Qian Yuezhi broadened them to three hundred sixty—this contradicts the Yellow Emperor's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's school expanded them to sixty, and Qian Yuezhi broadened them to 360—both contradict the Yellow Emperor's doctrine.

sentences.zh: 蓋樂之用《淮南》之術，一律而生五音，十二律而為六十音，而六之，故三百六十音，以當一歲之日。

translations.literal: Music employed the method of the Huainanzi: one pitch standard generates five tones, twelve pitch standards make sixty tones, and multiplied by six there are three hundred sixty tones to match the days of one year.
translations.idiomatic: Music adopted the method of the Huainanzi: one pitch standard generates five tones; twelve standards yield sixty tones; multiplied by six, this gives 360 tones to correspond to the days of the year.

sentences.zh: 以黃鐘、太蔟、姑洗、林鐘、南呂生三十有四，以大呂、夾鐘、中呂、蕤賓、夷則、無射生二十有七，應鐘生二十有八，始于包育，而終於安運。

translations.literal: From Yellow Bell, Great Cluster, Maiden Wash, Forest Bell, and Southern Flaring thirty-four are generated; from Great Clarity, Pinched Bell, Middle Clarity, Flaring Guest, Leveling Tone, and Unpitched twenty-seven; from Responding Bell twenty-eight—beginning at Bao Yu and ending at An Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell, Great Cluster, Maiden Wash, Forest Bell, and Southern Flaring generate thirty-four; Great Clarity, Pinched Bell, Middle Clarity, Flaring Guest, Leveling Tone, and Unpitched generate twenty-seven; Responding Bell generates twenty-eight—beginning with Bao Yu and ending with An Yun.

sentences.zh: 然由黃鐘迄於壯進百有五十，則三分損一焉以下生；

translations.literal: From Yellow Bell to Zhuang Jin one hundred fifty, one diminishes by one-third for lower generation;
translations.idiomatic: From Yellow Bell through Zhuang Jin there are 150 tones generated by diminishing one-third for lower generation;

sentences.zh: 由依行迄於億兆二百有九，則三分益一焉以上生；

translations.literal: from Yi Xing to Yi Zhao two hundred nine, one augments by one-third for upper generation;
translations.idiomatic: from Yi Xing through Yi Zhao there are 209 tones generated by augmenting one-third for upper generation;

sentences.zh: 惟安運為終而不生。

translations.literal: only An Yun is the end and generates no more.
translations.idiomatic: only An Yun is terminal and generates no further tone.

sentences.zh: 其言與黃帝之法大相牴牾。

translations.literal: Their words greatly contradict the Yellow Emperor's method.
translations.idiomatic: Their doctrine sharply contradicts the Yellow Emperor's method.

sentences.zh: 自遷、固而下，至是雜然莫適為主，至五季王樸而後議少定，沈括、蔣之奇論之當矣。

translations.literal: From Qian and Gu downward, by this time diverse views had no settled master; only in the Five Dynasties did Wang Pu bring debate somewhat to rest, and Shen Kuo and Jiang Zhiqi argued correctly.
translations.idiomatic: From Sima Qian and Ban Gu onward, theories proliferated with no settled authority until Wang Pu in the Five Dynasties brought debate somewhat to rest; Shen Kuo and Jiang Zhiqi then argued the matter correctly.

sentences.zh: 是不亦汨其泥而揚其波乎？

translations.literal: Is this not also muddling their silt and raising their waves?
translations.idiomatic: Did they not stir the mud and send the waves still higher?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 律也者，固以實為本而法為末，陛下修其實于上，而有司方定其法於下，以協天地中和之聲，則夫數子者，其說有可考焉，臣敢輕議哉！

translations.literal: Pitch standards take volume as root and method as branch; Your Majesty cultivates the volume above while the officials are just now fixing the method below, to harmonize with the neutral tone of heaven and earth—then those several masters' theories may be examined; how dare your servant lightly discuss them!
translations.idiomatic: Pitch standards take volumetric substance as fundamental and computational method as secondary; Your Majesty is refining the substance above while officials below are establishing the method, to harmonize with the balanced tones of heaven and earth. The theories of those masters may then be examined—how dare I presume to judge them lightly!

sentences.zh: 淳熙間，建安布衣蔡元定著《律呂新書》，朱熹稱其超然遠覽，奮其獨見，爬梳剔抉，參互考尋，推原本根，比次條理，管括機要，闡究精微。

translations.literal: In the Chunxi era, the Jian'an commoner Cai Yuanding wrote the New Book on Pitch Pipes; Zhu Xi praised him for transcendent far vision, vigorous independent insight, combing and sifting, cross-examining and seeking, tracing back to the root, arranging in order, encompassing essentials, and elucidating the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunxi era, Cai Yuanding of Jian'an, a man of no official rank, wrote the New Book on Pitch Pipes. Zhu Xi praised his far-reaching vision, his bold independent insights, his meticulous sifting of evidence, his cross-comparison of sources, his tracing of doctrines to their roots, his orderly arrangement of topics, his grasp of essentials, and his exposition of subtle points.

sentences.zh: 其言雖多出於近世之所未講，而實無一字不本于古人之成法。

translations.literal: His words, though mostly on what recent times had not discussed, in fact have not one character that does not rest on the ancients' established methods.
translations.idiomatic: Though much of what he wrote addressed topics neglected in recent times, not a single word failed to rest on the established methods of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其書有《律呂本原》、《律呂證辨》。

translations.literal: His book has Origins of Pitch Pipes and Evidential Analysis of Pitch Pipes.
translations.idiomatic: The work comprises Origins of Pitch Pipes and Evidential Analysis of Pitch Pipes.

sentences.zh: 《本原》者，《黃鐘》第一，《黃鐘之實》第二，《黃鐘生十二律》第三，《十二律之實》第四，《變律》第五，《律生五聲圖》第六，《變聲》第七，《八十四聲圖》第八，《六十調圖》第九，《候氣》第十，《審度》第十一，《嘉量》第十二，《謹權量》第十三。

translations.literal: Origins: Yellow Bell first, Volume of Yellow Bell second, Yellow Bell Generates the Twelve Pitch Standards third, Volumes of the Twelve Pitch Standards fourth, Variant Pitch Standards fifth, Diagram of Pitch Standards Generating Five Tones sixth, Variant Tones seventh, Diagram of Eighty-four Tones eighth, Diagram of Sixty Modes ninth, Awaiting Qi tenth, Examining Measures eleventh, Fine Capacity twelfth, Careful Weights and Measures thirteenth.
translations.idiomatic: Origins contains thirteen chapters: Yellow Bell; the Volumetric Standard of Yellow Bell; Yellow Bell Generates the Twelve Pitch Pipes; the Standards of the Twelve Pipes; Variant Pitch Pipes; Diagram of Pitch Pipes Generating the Five Tones; Variant Tones; Diagram of Eighty-four Tones; Diagram of Sixty Modes; Awaiting Qi; Examining Measures; Fine Capacity; and Careful Weights and Measures.

sentences.zh: 《證辨》者，《造律》第一，《律長短圍徑之數》第二，《黃鐘之實》第三，《三分損益上下相生》第四，《和聲》第五。

translations.literal: Evidential Analysis: Making Pitch Standards first, Numbers of Length, Circumference, and Diameter of Pitch Standards second, Volume of Yellow Bell third, Three-part Diminishment and Augmentation with Upper and Lower Generation fourth, Harmonious Sounds fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Evidential Analysis contains five chapters: Making Pitch Pipes; Numbers for Length, Circumference, and Diameter; the Volumetric Standard of Yellow Bell; Three-part Diminishment and Augmentation with Upper and Lower Generation; and Harmonious Sounds.

sentences.zh: 權臣既誣元定以偽學，貶死舂陵，雖有其書，卒為空言，嗚呼惜哉！

translations.literal: Powerful ministers slandered Yuanding as heterodox learning; he was banished and died at Chunling—though his book exists, it ended as empty words. Alas, what a pity!
translations.idiomatic: Powerful ministers denounced Yuanding for heterodox learning; he was exiled and died at Chunling. Though his book survives, it remained mere words on the page—alas, what a loss!

sentences.zh: 久之，宜春歐陽之秀復著《律通》，其自序曰：

translations.literal: After a long while, Ouyang Zhixiu of Yichun again wrote Comprehensive Pitch Theory; his preface says:
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, Ouyang Zhixiu of Yichun wrote Comprehensive Pitch Theory, in whose preface he states:

sentences.zh: 自律呂之度數不見於經，而釋經者反援《漢志》以為據，蓋濫觴于《管子》、《呂氏春秋》，流衍於《淮南子》、司馬遷之書，而波助于劉歆、京房之學。

translations.literal: Since the numbers of pitch pipes do not appear in the classics, yet classicists in explaining the classics instead cite the Han Treatises as authority—this first trickled from Guanzi and Lüshi Chunqiu, spread through Huainanzi and Sima Qian's book, and was aided by the waves of Liu Xin and Jing Fang's learning.
translations.idiomatic: Because the numerical measures of pitch pipes do not appear in the canonical classics, commentators have instead cited the Han Treatises as authority—a doctrine that first trickled from Guanzi and Lüshi Chunqiu, spread through Huainanzi and Sima Qian, and was carried forward by Liu Xin and Jing Fang.

sentences.zh: 班固《漢志》，盡歆所出也；

translations.literal: Ban Gu's Han Treatises—all came from Xin;
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's Han Treatises were entirely the work of Liu Xin;

sentences.zh: 《司馬彪志》，盡房所出也。

translations.literal: Sima Biao's Treatises—all came from Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao's Treatises were entirely the work of Jing Fang.

sentences.zh: 後世協律者，類皆執守以為定法。

translations.literal: Later harmonizers of pitch standards all clung to these as fixed methods.
translations.idiomatic: Later harmonizers of pitch pipes all clung to these as fixed law.

sentences.zh: 歷代合樂，不為無人，而終不足以得天地陰陽之和聲，所以不能追還于隆古之盛者，大抵由三分損益之說拘之也。

translations.literal: Through the dynasties in harmonizing music there were not lacking men, yet they never sufficed to obtain the harmonious sounds of heaven and earth's yin and yang; the reason they could not return to the grandeur of high antiquity lay largely in being constrained by the three-part diminishment and augmentation theory.
translations.idiomatic: Each dynasty had its experts in harmonizing music, yet none succeeded in attaining the balanced tones of heaven and earth's yin and yang; the reason they could not restore the splendor of high antiquity lay largely in their bondage to the three-part diminishment-and-augmentation theory.

sentences.zh: 夫律固不能舍損益之說以求之，由其有損有益，而後有上生下生之異。

translations.literal: Pitch standards indeed cannot be sought apart from diminishment and augmentation theory; because there is diminishment and augmentation, there afterward arise the differences of upper and lower generation.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch pipes cannot be derived without diminishment and augmentation; it is through diminishment and augmentation that upper and lower generation arise.

sentences.zh: 至其專用三分以為損益之法則失之，未免乎聲與數之不相合，有非天成之自然耳。

translations.literal: As for exclusively using three parts as the method of diminishment and augmentation, that is erroneous—sound and number inevitably fail to accord, falling short of heaven's natural endowment.
translations.idiomatic: But to rely exclusively on one-third as the method of diminishment and augmentation is an error; sound and number inevitably fail to align, falling short of what heaven endowed by nature.

sentences.zh: 蓋嘗因其損益、上下生之義，而去其專用三分之蔽，乃多為分法以求之，自黃鐘以往，其下生者盈十，而上生者止一而已。

translations.literal: I have followed the meaning of diminishment, augmentation, and upper and lower generation, removing the obscuration of exclusive use of three parts, and made many fractional methods to seek them—from Yellow Bell onward, lower generations exceed ten while upper generation stops at one alone.
translations.idiomatic: I have followed the principles of diminishment, augmentation, and upper and lower generation while discarding the error of relying solely on one-third, and devised many fractional methods of calculation. From Yellow Bell onward, lower generations number more than ten, while upper generation occurs only once.

sentences.zh: 此其數之或損或益，出於自然，而與舊法固不侔矣。

translations.literal: These numbers, whether diminished or augmented, arise from nature and are inherently unlike the old method.
translations.idiomatic: Whether these numbers are diminished or augmented, they arise from nature and are fundamentally unlike the old method.

sentences.zh: 若謂相生之法，一下必一上，既上而復下，則其法之窮也，於蕤賓、大呂間見之。

translations.literal: If one says the method of mutual generation requires one lower after every upper, and after upper again lower, then the method reaches its limit—this is seen between Flaring Guest and Great Clarity.
translations.idiomatic: If one insists that generation must alternate lower and upper without exception, the method reaches its limit—and that limit appears between Flaring Guest and Great Clarity.

sentences.zh: 夫黃鐘而降，轉以相生，至於姑洗則下生應鐘，而應鐘之上生蕤賓者，法也。

translations.literal: From Yellow Bell downward, turning by mutual generation, reaching Maiden Wash one lower-generates Responding Bell, and Responding Bell upper-generating Flaring Guest is the method.
translations.idiomatic: From Yellow Bell downward, pipes are generated in succession; at Maiden Wash one lower-generates Responding Bell, and Responding Bell upper-generates Flaring Guest—this is the standard method.

sentences.zh: 今乃蕤賓之生大呂，又從而上生焉，此《班志》所載，所以變其說為下生大呂，而大呂之長遂用倍法矣。

translations.literal: Now Flaring Guest generates Great Clarity, yet again upper-generates—this is what Ban's Treatises record; hence they changed the theory to lower-generate Great Clarity, and Great Clarity's length then used the doubling method.
translations.idiomatic: Yet here Flaring Guest generates Great Clarity by upper generation again—this is what Ban's Treatises record, which is why they revised the theory to lower-generate Great Clarity and applied the doubling method to Great Clarity's length.

sentences.zh: 夫律之相生而用倍法，猶為有理，獨專用三分以為損益，則律之長短，不中乎天地自然之數爾。

translations.literal: For pitch standards to generate one another using the doubling method is still reasonable; only exclusive use of three parts for diminishment and augmentation makes the lengths of pitch standards fail to hit heaven and earth's natural numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Using the doubling method in pitch generation is still defensible; it is exclusive reliance on one-third for diminishment and augmentation that makes pipe lengths fail to match heaven and earth's natural proportions.

sentences.zh: 生律之分，蓋不止於三分損益之一端，以一律而分為三，此生律之極數，特一求徵聲之法耳。

translations.literal: The fractions for generating pitch standards are not limited to the one avenue of three-part diminishment and augmentation; dividing one pitch standard into three is the extreme number for generation—merely one method for seeking the fifth tone.
translations.idiomatic: The fractional divisions for generating pitch pipes are not limited to three-part diminishment and augmentation alone; dividing one pipe into three parts is the ultimate fractional division—merely one method for deriving the fifth tone.

sentences.zh: 苟以三分損益，一下生而一上生，則聲律殆無窮矣，何至於十二而止也乎。

translations.literal: If with three-part diminishment and augmentation one lower-generates and one upper-generates alternately, tones and pitch standards would be nearly endless—how could they stop at twelve?
translations.idiomatic: If one applied three-part diminishment and augmentation with strict alternation of lower and upper generation, tones would be nearly infinite—how could the series stop at twelve?

sentences.zh: 夫十二律之生也，十律皆下生，一律獨上生。

translations.literal: In the generation of the twelve pitch standards, ten standards are all lower-generated, one standard alone is upper-generated.
translations.idiomatic: Of the twelve pitch pipes, ten are generated by lower generation and only one by upper generation.

sentences.zh: 唯其下生者，損之極也，而後上生者益焉。

translations.literal: Only when lower generation reaches the extreme of diminishment does upper generation then augment.
translations.idiomatic: Only when lower generation has diminished to the extreme does upper generation augment.

sentences.zh: 上生則律窮矣，此窮上反下、窮下反上之理也。

translations.literal: Upper generation then exhausts the pitch standards—this is the principle of exhausted above returning below, exhausted below returning above.
translations.idiomatic: Upper generation then exhausts the series—this is the principle that when the upper limit is reached one returns downward, and when the lower limit is reached one returns upward.

sentences.zh: 琴一弦之間具十二律，皆用下生之法，而末以上生法終之。

translations.literal: On one string of the qin the twelve pitch standards are all present—all use lower-generation method, and at the end upper-generation method concludes it.
translations.idiomatic: On a single qin string all twelve pitch pipes are present, all produced by lower generation, with upper generation applied only at the end.

sentences.zh: 若以七弦而緊慢之為旋宮之法，則應鐘一均之律，宮聲之外，多用倍法生一律矣。

translations.literal: If with seven strings one tightens and loosens them as the method of rotating the palace tone, then within one scale of Responding Bell, beyond the palace tone one mostly uses the doubling method to generate one pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: If the seven strings are tightened and loosened as the method of mode rotation, then within the Responding Bell scale, beyond the foundation tone the doubling method is often used to generate additional pipes.

sentences.zh: 此天地聲音自然而然，不可拘於一而不知通變也。

translations.literal: This is heaven and earth's sounds coming naturally of themselves—one cannot be constrained to one method without knowing how to adapt.
translations.idiomatic: This reflects how the sounds of heaven and earth arise naturally—one cannot cling to a single fixed rule without understanding adaptation.

sentences.zh: 故正律止於十二而已。

translations.literal: Thus the correct pitch standards stop at twelve alone.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the canonical pitch pipes number twelve and no more.

sentences.zh: 竊意十二律之度數，當具于《周禮》之《冬官》，如《考工記》鳧氏為鐘、磬氏為磬之類，各有一職。

translations.literal: I suspect the numbers of the twelve pitch standards ought to have been complete in the Winter Offices of the Rites of Zhou, like in the Artificers' Record where the Wild-Goose clan made bells and the Chime-stone clan made chime-stones—each had its office.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect the numerical measures of the twelve pitch pipes were fully recorded in the Winter Offices section of the Rites of Zhou, as in the Artificers' Record where the Wild-Goose clan fashioned bells and the Chime-stone clan fashioned sonorous stones—each craft had its specialist.

sentences.zh: 然《冬官》一篇既亡，則世無以考其度數之詳，而三分損益之說散見於書傳者，恐或得之目擊而不及識其全，或得之口授而未能究其誤，或求諸耳決而不能究其真，因是遂著為定論。

translations.literal: Yet with the Winter Offices chapter already lost, the world has no means to examine the details of its numbers; the three-part diminishment and augmentation theory scattered in books and transmissions—perhaps some obtained it by eyewitness without grasping the whole, some by oral transmission without investigating errors, some by ear judgment without pursuing the truth—thus it was fixed as settled doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: But with the Winter Offices chapter lost, the world could no longer verify the detailed measures. The three-part diminishment-and-augmentation theory scattered through transmitted texts may have been grasped by eyewitness without understanding the whole, received orally without tracing errors, or judged by ear without reaching the truth—thus it was enshrined as settled doctrine.

sentences.zh: 夫人皆以為法之盡善矣，豈知三分損益所生之律，乃僅得其聲之近似而未真。

translations.literal: People all thought the method perfectly good—how could they know that pitch standards generated by three-part diminishment and augmentation only obtained approximate sound, not the true?
translations.idiomatic: Everyone assumed the method was perfect—who knew that pitch pipes generated by three-part diminishment and augmentation only approximate the true sound?

sentences.zh: 蓋非師曠之聰，則耳不能齊，其聲之近似者，足以惑人之聽，是以不復求其法之未盡善者。

translations.literal: Unless one has Shi Kuang's acuity, the ear cannot align; sounds that approximate suffice to confuse human hearing—thus people no longer sought where the method was not perfectly good.
translations.idiomatic: Without Shi Kuang's acuity of hearing, the ear cannot discriminate precisely; sounds that merely approximate are enough to deceive the listener—so no one sought to improve a method that was not truly perfect.

sentences.zh: 此蔡邕所以不如耳決之明者，亦不能盡信其法也。

translations.literal: This is why Cai Yong, inferior to the clarity of ear judgment, also could not fully trust the method.
translations.idiomatic: This is why even Cai Yong, who fell short of the clarity of ear-based judgment, could not fully trust the method.

sentences.zh: 後世之制樂者，不知律法之固有未善，而每患其聲音高下之不協，以至取古昔遺亡之器而求之，蓋亦不知本矣。

translations.literal: Later makers of music, not knowing that pitch law was inherently imperfect, yet always worried that sounds high and low did not harmonize—even seeking ancient lost instruments—also did not know the root.
translations.idiomatic: Later composers of music, unaware that pitch theory was inherently flawed, worried instead that high and low tones failed to harmonize, and even sought out ancient instruments long lost—missing the root of the problem entirely.

sentences.zh: 聲以數而傳，數以聲而定，二者皆有自然之則。

translations.literal: Sound is transmitted by number, number is fixed by sound—both have natural principles.
translations.idiomatic: Sound is conveyed through number, and number is established through sound—each follows natural principles.

sentences.zh: 如侈者聲必咋，弇者聲必郁，高者數必短，下者數必長。

translations.literal: If enlarged, sound must be harsh; if constricted, sound must be muffled; if high, number must be short; if low, number must be long.
translations.idiomatic: An enlarged pipe produces a harsh tone; a constricted pipe a muffled one; a high tone corresponds to a short measure; a low tone to a long one.

sentences.zh: 侈弇者，數也，未聞其聲而已知其有咋鬱之分；

translations.literal: Enlargement and constriction are numbers—before hearing the sound one already knows it has harsh and muffled distinctions;
translations.idiomatic: Enlargement and constriction are matters of measure—before hearing the sound one can tell whether it will be harsh or muffled;

sentences.zh: 高下者，聲也，未見其數已知其有長短之異。

translations.literal: high and low are sound—before seeing the number one already knows it has long and short differences.
translations.idiomatic: high and low are matters of sound—before examining the measure one knows whether it will be long or short.

sentences.zh: 故不得其自然之聲，則數不可得而考；

translations.literal: Thus without obtaining its natural sound, the number cannot be examined;
translations.idiomatic: Thus without obtaining the natural sound, the numerical measure cannot be verified;

sentences.zh: 不得其自然之數，則聲不可得而言。

translations.literal: Without obtaining its natural number, sound cannot be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: without obtaining the natural measure, sound cannot be properly described.

sentences.zh: 今之制律者，不知出此，而顧先區區於秬黍之縱橫、古尺之修短、斛鬥之廣狹、鐘磬之高下謀之，是何足以得其聲之和哉！

translations.literal: Today's makers of pitch standards do not know to proceed from this, yet fuss first over the vertical and horizontal of black millet, the long and short of ancient feet, the wide and narrow of hu and dou, the high and low of bells and chime-stones—how could this suffice to obtain harmonious sound!
translations.idiomatic: Today's pipe-makers fail to grasp this principle, yet fuss over the orientation of black millet grains, the length of ancient rulers, the capacity of hu and dou measures, and the height of bells and chime-stones—how could such concerns ever yield harmonious sound!

sentences.zh: 邵雍曰：「世人所見者，漢律曆耳。」

translations.literal: Shao Yong said: "What people of the world see is only the Han pitch standards and calendar."
translations.idiomatic: Shao Yong remarked: "What the world knows is only the Han pitch standards and calendar."

sentences.zh: 然則三分損益之法為未善，亦隱然矣。

translations.literal: Thus that the three-part diminishment and augmentation method is not yet good is also implicitly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is implicitly clear that the three-part diminishment-and-augmentation method is imperfect.

sentences.zh: 近世蔡元定特著一書，可謂究心，然其說亦有可用與否。

translations.literal: In recent times Cai Yuanding specially wrote a book—one may call it devoted study—yet his theory also has what is usable and what is not.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times Cai Yuanding devoted himself to a special treatise, which shows genuine dedication; yet his theories too have their sound and unsound parts.

sentences.zh: 其可用者，多其所自得，而又有證于古，凡載於吾書者可見矣；

translations.literal: What is usable mostly comes from his own attainments and also has proof from antiquity—as may be seen in all recorded in my book;
translations.idiomatic: What is sound in his work largely reflects his own insights, corroborated by antiquity, as my book demonstrates;

sentences.zh: 其否者，皆由習熟於三分上下生之說，而不於聲器之近似者察之也。

translations.literal: what is not acceptable all stems from being practiced in the three-part upper and lower generation theory, without examining approximations in sound and instruments.
translations.idiomatic: what is unsound stems from his familiarity with three-part upper-and-lower generation theory, without scrutinizing how closely sounds and instruments actually match.

sentences.zh: 豈嘗察之而未有法以易之乎？

translations.literal: Had he ever examined it and found no method to replace it?
translations.idiomatic: Had he truly examined the matter and found no method to replace it?

sentences.zh: 此《律通》之所以作也。

translations.literal: This is why Comprehensive Pitch Theory was written.
translations.idiomatic: This is why I wrote Comprehensive Pitch Theory.

sentences.zh: 蓋律之所以長短，不止乎三分損益之一端，自四分以往，推而至於有二十分之法。

translations.literal: The reason pitch standards are long or short is not limited to the one avenue of three-part diminishment and augmentation—from four parts onward, extending even to methods of twenty parts.
translations.idiomatic: Pipe lengths are determined by more than three-part diminishment and augmentation alone—from four parts onward, the method extends even to twenty-part divisions.

sentences.zh: 管之所以廣狹，必限於千二百黍之定數，因其容受有方分、圜分之異，與黍體不相合，而遂分辨其空龠有實積、隙積之理。

translations.literal: The reason tubes are wide or narrow must be limited to the fixed number of one thousand two hundred grains of millet; because their capacity has differences of square parts and circular parts, not matching the millet's form, one then distinguishes the principle of empty yue having solid accumulation and gap accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Tube width must be tied to the fixed count of 1,200 millet grains; because capacity differs between square and circular measures and does not match the grain's form, one must distinguish between solid volume and interstitial volume within the empty yue.

sentences.zh: 其還相為宮之法，有以推見其為一陰一陽相繼之道，而非一上一下相生之謂也。

translations.literal: The method of mutually becoming palace tones can be inferred to show the way of one yin and one yang succeeding each other—not the meaning of one upper and one lower generating each other.
translations.idiomatic: The method of mode rotation reveals a succession of yin and yang tones—not mere alternation of upper and lower generation.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 觀吾書者，能知其數之出於自然而然，則知由先漢以前至於今日，上下幾二千年，凡史傳所述三分損益一定之說者，可以刪而去之矣。

translations.literal: Readers of my book who can know that its numbers arise from natural spontaneity will know that from before the Former Han to today, nearly two thousand years up and down—all historical accounts describing the fixed three-part diminishment and augmentation theory—may be deleted and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Readers who grasp that these numbers arise from natural spontaneity will see that for nearly two thousand years, from pre-Han times to the present, all historical accounts treating three-part diminishment and augmentation as fixed doctrine may be discarded.

sentences.zh: 使其說之可用也，則累世律可協、樂可和，何承天、劉焯輩不改其法矣。

translations.literal: If their theory were usable, then through successive generations pitch standards could harmonize and music could accord—why did He Chengtian, Liu Zhuo, and the like not change their method?
translations.idiomatic: If that theory were sound, successive generations would have achieved harmonious pitch and music—why then did He Chengtian, Liu Zhuo, and others revise the method?

sentences.zh: 故京房六十律不足以和樂，而況錢樂之衍為三百六十之非法，徒增多而無用乎？

translations.literal: Thus Jing Fang's sixty pitch standards were insufficient to harmonize music—how much more Qian Yuezhi's extension to the irregular three hundred sixty, merely increasing numbers without use?
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's sixty pitch pipes failed to harmonize music—how much less useful was Qian Yuezhi's expansion to an irregular 360, which merely multiplied numbers to no purpose?

sentences.zh: 是其數非出於自然之無所加損，而徒欲傅會於當期之日數雲爾。

translations.literal: Their numbers did not arise from nature's having nothing added or diminished, but merely wished to force-fit the day-count of the current period—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Their numbers did not arise from nature without addition or diminution, but merely forced a fit with the day-count of their own era.

sentences.zh: 古之聖人所以定律止於十二者，自然之理數也。

translations.literal: Why the ancient sages fixed pitch standards at twelve is the natural principle of numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The reason the ancient sages fixed pitch pipes at twelve lies in the natural order of numbers.

sentences.zh: 苟不因自然之理數，則以三分損益之法衍之，聲律殆不特三百六十而已也，而況京房之六十乎！

translations.literal: If not following the natural principle of numbers, then extending by the three-part diminishment and augmentation method, tones and pitch standards would be nearly not only three hundred sixty—and how much more Jing Fang's sixty!
translations.idiomatic: Without following natural numerical principles, extending the three-part method would yield far more than 360 tones—let alone Jing Fang's sixty!

sentences.zh: 且房之律，吾意其自為之也，而托言受之焦延壽，以欺乎人，以售其說。

translations.literal: Moreover, Fang's pitch standards—I suspect he made them himself, yet claimed to receive them from Jiao Yanshou, to deceive people and sell his theory.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I suspect Jing Fang devised his pitch pipes himself, then claimed to have received them from Jiao Yanshou in order to deceive the public and promote his theory.

sentences.zh: 使律法之善，何必曰受諸人？

translations.literal: If pitch law is good, why must one say it was received from others?
translations.idiomatic: If pitch theory is sound, why claim it was received from another?

sentences.zh: 律法不善矣，雖焦延壽何益哉！

translations.literal: If pitch law is not good, even Jiao Yanshou is of what use!
translations.idiomatic: If pitch theory is unsound, what good is Jiao Yanshou's authority?

sentences.zh: 所謂善不善者，亦顧其法之可用與否耳。

translations.literal: What is called good or not good also depends on whether the method is usable or not.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a theory is sound depends solely on whether its method works.

sentences.zh: 曩者，魏漢津嘗創用指尺以制律，乃竊京房之故智，上以取君之信，下以遏人之議，能行之於一日，豈能使一世而用之乎？

translations.literal: Formerly Wei Hanjin once innovated using finger-length to make pitch standards—he merely stole Jing Fang's old trick, above to gain the ruler's trust, below to suppress people's criticism; able to implement it for one day, could he make the world use it?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Wei Hanjin innovated by using finger-length to fashion pitch pipes—merely stealing Jing Fang's old trick to win the ruler's trust above and silence critics below. He could enforce it for a day, but could he make the world adopt it?

sentences.zh: 今《律通》之作，其數之損益可以互相生，總為百四十四以為之體，或變之，又可得二百一十有六以為之用，乾坤之策具矣。

translations.literal: Now in writing Comprehensive Pitch Theory, its numbers of diminishment and augmentation can mutually generate, totaling one hundred forty-four as the substance; or transformed, one can further obtain two hundred sixteen for use—the policies of Qian and Kun are complete.
translations.idiomatic: In Comprehensive Pitch Theory, the diminished and augmented numbers mutually generate: 144 form the substance, and with transformation yield 216 for practical use—the numbers of Qian and Kun are complete.

sentences.zh: 世不用則已，用則聲必和，亦因古黃鐘九寸法審之，以人物之聲而稍更定之耳。

translations.literal: If the world does not use it, so be it; if used, sound must harmonize—it also follows the ancient Yellow Bell nine-inch method for examination, slightly readjusting according to human and material sounds.
translations.idiomatic: If the world ignores it, so be it; if adopted, sound will harmonize. The method follows the ancient nine-inch Yellow Bell standard, adjusted slightly according to actual human and instrumental tones.

sentences.zh: 或曰：律止十二，胡為復衍百四十四律乎？」

translations.literal: Someone said: Pitch standards stop at twelve—why extend again to one hundred forty-four pitch standards?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "Pitch pipes number only twelve—why derive 144 additional pipes?"

sentences.zh: 應之曰：「十二者，正聲也；

translations.literal: He answered: "Twelve are correct tones;
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Twelve are the primary tones;

sentences.zh: 百四十四者，變聲也。

translations.literal: one hundred forty-four are variant tones.
translations.idiomatic: 144 are variant tones.

sentences.zh: 使不為百四十四者，何以見十二宮七聲長短之有定數，而宮、商、角、徵、羽清濁之有定分乎？

translations.literal: If there were not one hundred forty-four, how could one see the fixed numbers for the long and short of twelve palace tones and seven sounds, and the fixed divisions of palace, commercial, horn, fifth, and feather clear and muddy?
translations.idiomatic: Without the 144, how could one discern the fixed proportions of length among the twelve modes and seven tones, or the fixed distinctions of clear and muddy among gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu?

sentences.zh: 其要主於和而已。

translations.literal: The essential lies in harmony alone.
translations.idiomatic: The essential point is harmony alone.

sentences.zh: 故有正聲則有變聲也，通其變然後可與論律矣。」

translations.literal: Thus with correct tones there are variant tones; penetrating the variants, one may then discuss pitch standards."
translations.idiomatic: Where there are primary tones there must be variant tones; only by mastering the variants can one truly discuss pitch theory."

sentences.zh: 《律通》上、下二篇：《十二律名數》第一，《黃鐘起數》第二，《生律分正法》第三，《生律分變法》第四，《正變生律分起演算法》第五，《十二宮百四十四律數》第六，《律數傍通法》第七，《律數傍通別法》第八；

translations.literal: Comprehensive Pitch Theory in two parts, upper and lower: Names and Numbers of the Twelve Pitch Standards first, Starting Numbers from Yellow Bell second, Correct Method of Fractions for Generating Pitch Standards third, Variant Method of Fractions for Generating Pitch Standards fourth, Algorithm for Deriving Correct and Variant Fractions fifth, Numbers of One Hundred Forty-four Pitch Standards in Twelve Palaces sixth, Method of Pitch Numbers Mutually Penetrating seventh, Separate Method of Pitch Numbers Mutually Penetrating eighth;
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Pitch Theory comprises two parts. The first eight chapters are: Names and Numbers of the Twelve Pitch Pipes; Starting Numbers from Yellow Bell; Correct Method of Fractional Generation; Variant Method of Fractional Generation; Algorithm for Deriving Correct and Variant Fractions; Numbers of 144 Pipes in Twelve Modes; Method of Interpenetrating Pitch Numbers; and Separate Method of Interpenetrating Pitch Numbers;

sentences.zh: 《九分為寸法辨》第九、第十，《五十九律會同》第十一，《空圍龠實辨》第十二，《十二律分陰陽圖說》第十三，《陽聲陰聲配乾坤圖》第十四，《五聲配五行之序》第十五，《七聲配五行之序》第十六，《七聲分類》第十七，《十二宮七聲倡和》第十八，《六十調圖說》第十九，《辨三律聲法》第二十。

translations.literal: Discourse on Nine Parts Making One Inch ninth and tenth, Concordance of Fifty-nine Pitch Standards eleventh, Discourse on Empty Circumference and Yue Volume twelfth, Diagrammatic Explanation of Twelve Pitch Standards Divided into Yin and Yang thirteenth, Diagram Matching Yang and Yin Sounds to Qian and Kun fourteenth, Sequence of Five Sounds Matching Five Phases fifteenth, Sequence of Seven Sounds Matching Five Phases sixteenth, Classification of Seven Sounds seventeenth, Mutual Responsiveness of Twelve Palaces and Seven Sounds eighteenth, Diagrammatic Explanation of Sixty Modes nineteenth, Discerning Three Pitch Standard Sound Methods twentieth.
translations.idiomatic: followed by: Discourse on Nine Parts per Inch (chapters 9–10); Concordance of Fifty-nine Pitch Pipes; Discourse on Empty Circumference and Yue Volume; Diagram of Twelve Pipes Divided into Yin and Yang; Diagram Matching Yang and Yin Tones to Qian and Kun; Sequence of Five Tones and the Five Phases; Sequence of Seven Tones and the Five Phases; Classification of Seven Tones; Mutual Responsiveness of Twelve Modes and Seven Tones; Diagram of Sixty Modes; and Discerning Three Pitch Sound Methods.

sentences.zh: 真德秀、趙以夫皆盛稱之。

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu and Zhao Yifu both lavishly praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu and Zhao Yifu both praised it highly.

sentences.zh: 舒州桐城縣丞李如篪作《樂書》，評司馬光、範鎮所論律，曰：

translations.literal: Li Ruchi, assistant magistrate of Tongcheng County in Shuzhou, wrote the Book of Music, evaluating Sima Guang and Fan Zhen's discussions of pitch standards, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruchi, assistant magistrate of Tongcheng in Shuzhou, wrote the Book of Music, in which he evaluates Sima Guang and Fan Zhen's debates on pitch standards:

sentences.zh: 鎮得蜀人房庶言尺法，庶言：「嘗得古本《漢書》，云：'度起于黃鐘之長，以子穀秬黍中者，一黍之起，積一千二百黍之廣，度之九十分，黃鐘之長，一為一分。

translations.literal: Zhen obtained the foot-measure method from Fang Shu of Shu; Fang said: "I once obtained an ancient edition of the Book of Han, which says: 'Measure arises from the length of Yellow Bell; using black millet of Zi Valley of medium size, one grain's height, accumulated to the breadth of one thousand two hundred grains, measured to ninety parts—Yellow Bell's length, one serving as one part.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen obtained the foot-measure method from Fang Shu of Shu, who said: "I once obtained an ancient edition of the Book of Han stating: 'Measure arises from the length of Yellow Bell; using medium black millet from Zi Valley, the height of one grain, accumulated to the breadth of 1,200 grains, measured to ninety parts—the length of Yellow Bell, one part.

sentences.zh: '今文脫去'之起積一千二百黍'八字，故自前世累黍為之，縱置之則太長，橫置之則太短。

translations.literal: ' The present text omits the eight characters 'height accumulated to one thousand two hundred grains'—thus from former generations people stacked grains for this; placed vertically it is too long, placed horizontally too short.
translations.idiomatic: The present text omits the eight characters 'height accumulated to 1,200 grains.' Hence from former times people stacked grains to measure; placed vertically the result was too long, horizontally too short.

sentences.zh: 今新尺橫置之不能容一千二百黍，則大其空徑四厘六毫，是以樂聲太高，皆由儒者誤以一黍為一分，其法非是。

translations.literal: Now the new foot placed horizontally cannot contain one thousand two hundred grains—so they enlarged the empty diameter by four li six hao; thus musical sound is too high—all because Confucian scholars mistakenly took one grain as one part; their method is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The new foot measure laid horizontally cannot hold 1,200 grains, so they enlarged the inner diameter by 0.046 units—making musical tones too high—all because scholars mistakenly treated one grain as one part. Their method is wrong.

sentences.zh: 不若以千二百黍實管中，隨其短長斷之，以為黃鐘九寸之管九十分，其長一為一分，取三分以度空徑，數合則律正矣。」

translations.literal: Better to fill the tube with one thousand two hundred grains, cut it according to its short or long length, making the Yellow Bell nine-inch tube ninety parts with its length one as one part; take three parts to measure the empty diameter—when numbers accord, pitch standards are correct."
translations.idiomatic: Better to fill the pipe with 1,200 grains, cut it to the appropriate length, and take the nine-inch Yellow Bell pipe as ninety parts, one part equaling one unit of length; use three parts to measure the inner diameter—when the numbers align, the pitch is correct."

sentences.zh: 鎮盛稱此論，以為先儒用意皆不能到。

translations.literal: Zhen lavishly praised this theory, thinking former Confucians' intentions could not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen praised this theory highly, believing earlier Confucian scholars had never grasped the point.

sentences.zh: 其意謂制律之法，必以一千二百黍實黃鐘九寸之管九十分，其管之長一為一分，是度由律起也。

translations.literal: His meaning is that the method of making pitch standards must fill the Yellow Bell nine-inch tube's ninety parts with one thousand two hundred grains, the tube's length one serving as one part—measure arises from pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: His view is that pitch pipes must be made by filling the nine-inch Yellow Bell pipe (ninety parts, one part equaling one unit of length) with 1,200 grains—measure arises from pitch.

sentences.zh: 光則據《漢書》正本之「度起于黃鐘之長。

translations.literal: Guang then relied on the correct edition of the Book of Han: "Measure arises from the length of Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang relied on the standard edition of the Book of Han: "Measure arises from the length of Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 以子穀秬黍中者，一黍之廣，度之九十分，黃鐘之長，一為一分。」

translations.literal: Using black millet of Zi Valley of medium size, one grain's breadth, measured to ninety parts—Yellow Bell's length, one serving as one part."
translations.idiomatic: Using medium black millet from Zi Valley, the breadth of one grain, measured to ninety parts—the length of Yellow Bell, one part."

sentences.zh: 本無「之起積一千二百黍」八字。

translations.literal: Originally there were no eight characters 'height accumulated to one thousand two hundred grains.'
translations.idiomatic: The original text contains no phrase 'height accumulated to 1,200 grains.'

sentences.zh: 其意謂制律之法，必以一黍之廣定為一分，九十分則得黃鐘之長，是律由度起也。

translations.literal: His meaning is that the method of making pitch standards must fix one grain's breadth as one part; ninety parts then obtain Yellow Bell's length—pitch standards arise from measure.
translations.idiomatic: His view is that pitch pipes must be made by fixing the breadth of one grain as one part; ninety parts yield the length of Yellow Bell—pitch arises from measure.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「同律、度、量、衡。」

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Harmonize pitch standards, measure, quantity, and balance."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents states: "Harmonize pitch, measure, quantity, and weight."

sentences.zh: 先言律而後及度、量、衡，是度起於律，信矣。

translations.literal: Speaking of pitch standards first and afterward measure, quantity, and balance—measure arises from pitch standards, truly.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch is named before measure, quantity, and weight—measure arises from pitch, beyond doubt.

sentences.zh: 然則鎮之說是，而光之說非也。

translations.literal: Thus Zhen's theory is correct and Guang's theory is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Fan Zhen is right and Sima Guang wrong.

sentences.zh: 然庶之論積一千二百黍之廣之說則非，必如其說，則是律非起於度而起於量也。

translations.literal: Yet Fang's theory of accumulating the breadth of one thousand two hundred grains is wrong; if one must follow his theory, then pitch standards do not arise from measure but from quantity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fang's theory of accumulating the breadth of 1,200 grains is wrong; if accepted, pitch would arise not from measure but from quantity.

sentences.zh: 光之說雖非先王作律之本，而後之為律者，不先定其分寸，亦無以起律。

translations.literal: Guang's theory, though not the root of the former kings' making pitch standards, yet for later makers of pitch standards, without first fixing their parts and inches, there is no means to establish pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang's method, though not how the ancient kings originally fashioned pitch pipes, is nonetheless necessary for later makers who cannot establish pitch without first fixing fractional measures.

sentences.zh: 又其法本之《漢志》之文，則光之說亦不得謂其非是也。

translations.literal: Moreover, since his method is rooted in the text of the Han Treatises, Guang's theory also cannot be called wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since his method rests on the Han Treatises, Sima Guang's view cannot simply be dismissed as wrong.

sentences.zh: 故嘗論之，律者，述氣之管也。

translations.literal: Thus I have discussed: pitch standards are tubes that convey qi.
translations.idiomatic: I have argued that pitch pipes are tubes that convey qi.

sentences.zh: 其候氣之法，十有二月，每月為管，置於地中。

translations.literal: The method of awaiting qi: twelve months, each month one tube, placed in the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The method of awaiting qi employs twelve tubes, one for each month, buried in the earth.

sentences.zh: 氣之來至，有淺有深，而管之入地者，有短有長。

translations.literal: Qi's arrival is shallow or deep, while the tube's penetration into earth is short or long.
translations.idiomatic: Qi arrives at varying depths, and the tubes are buried to varying lengths.

sentences.zh: 十二月之氣至，各驗其當月之管，氣至則灰飛也。

translations.literal: When the twelve months' qi arrives, each verifies its tube for that month—when qi arrives, ash flies.
translations.idiomatic: When each month's qi arrives, the corresponding tube is tested—when qi arrives, the ash flies up.

sentences.zh: 其為管之長短，與其氣至之淺深，或不相當則不驗。

translations.literal: If the tube's length and shortness does not match the qi's shallow and deep arrival, it is not verified.
translations.idiomatic: If the tube's length does not match the depth at which qi arrives, the test fails.

sentences.zh: 上古之聖人制為十二管，以候十二辰之氣，而十二辰之音亦由之而出焉。

translations.literal: The sages of high antiquity made twelve tubes to await the qi of the twelve branches, and the tones of the twelve branches also issued from them.
translations.idiomatic: The sages of high antiquity fashioned twelve tubes to await the qi of the twelve earthly branches, and the tones of those branches issued from them.

sentences.zh: 以十二管較之，則黃鐘之管最長，應鐘之管至短；

translations.literal: Comparing the twelve tubes, Yellow Bell's tube is longest, Responding Bell's tube shortest;
translations.idiomatic: Comparing the twelve tubes, Yellow Bell's is longest and Responding Bell's shortest;

sentences.zh: 以林鐘比于黃鐘，則短其三分之一；

translations.literal: comparing Forest Bell with Yellow Bell, it is one-third shorter;
translations.idiomatic: Forest Bell is one-third shorter than Yellow Bell;

sentences.zh: 乙太簇比之林鐘，則長其三分之一；

translations.literal: Great Cluster compared with Forest Bell is one-third longer;
translations.idiomatic: Great Cluster is one-third longer than Forest Bell;

sentences.zh: 其餘或長或短，皆上下於三分之一之數。

translations.literal: the rest, whether long or short, all rise and fall by the number of one-third.
translations.idiomatic: the remaining pipes vary in length, all by increments of one-third.

sentences.zh: 其默符于聲氣自然之應者如此也，當時惡睹所謂三分損益哉！

translations.literal: Thus they silently accorded with sound and qi's natural responsiveness—how could they then have seen what is called three-part diminishment and augmentation!
translations.idiomatic: They silently matched the natural correspondence of sound and qi—how could they have known anything of three-part diminishment and augmentation!

sentences.zh: 又惡睹夫一千二百黍實黃鐘容受之量與夫一黍之廣一為一分之說哉！

translations.literal: How could they have seen the theory of one thousand two hundred grains filling Yellow Bell's capacity, or one grain's breadth as one part!
translations.idiomatic: How could they have known the theory of 1,200 grains filling Yellow Bell, or of one grain's breadth as one part!

sentences.zh: 古之聖人既為律矣，欲因之以起度、量、衡之法，遂取秬黍之中者以實黃鐘之管，滿龠傾而數之，得黍一千有二百，因以制量；

translations.literal: The ancient sages, having made pitch standards, wished to derive from them methods for measure, quantity, and balance; they took medium black millet to fill Yellow Bell's tube, filled the yue and poured to count—obtaining one thousand two hundred grains, and thereby made quantity;
translations.idiomatic: Having fashioned pitch pipes, the ancient sages wished to derive measure, quantity, and weight from them. They took medium black millet, filled the Yellow Bell pipe, poured it into the yue and counted—obtaining 1,200 grains—and thereby established quantity;

sentences.zh: 以一黍之廣而度之，得黃鐘管九十分之一，因以起度；

translations.literal: measured one grain's breadth, obtaining one ninetieth of Yellow Bell's tube, and thereby established measure;
translations.idiomatic: measured the breadth of one grain to obtain one-ninetieth of the Yellow Bell pipe, and thereby established measure;

sentences.zh: 以一龠之黍之重而兩之，因以生衡。

translations.literal: doubled the weight of one yue's millet, and thereby generated balance.
translations.idiomatic: doubled the weight of millet in one yue, and thereby established weight.

sentences.zh: 去古既遠，先王作律之本始，其法不傳，而猶有所謂一千二百黍為一龠容受之量與夫一黍之廣一為一分者可考也。

translations.literal: Far from antiquity, the former kings' root of making pitch standards—its method is not transmitted—yet what is called one thousand two hundred grains as one yue's capacity and one grain's breadth as one part can still be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: The original method by which the former kings fashioned pitch pipes is lost, yet the capacity of 1,200 grains per yue and the breadth of one grain as one part can still be traced.

sentences.zh: 推其容受而度其分寸，則律可得而成也。

translations.literal: Inferring capacity and measuring parts and inches, pitch standards can then be completed.
translations.idiomatic: By inferring capacity and measuring fractional dimensions, pitch pipes can be fashioned.

sentences.zh: 先王之本於律以起度、量、衡者，自源而生流也；

translations.literal: The former kings' basing measure, quantity, and balance on pitch standards is generating the stream from the source;
translations.idiomatic: The former kings derived measure, quantity, and weight from pitch—flowing from source to stream;

sentences.zh: 後人以度、量、衡而起律者，尋流而及源也。

translations.literal: later people establishing pitch standards from measure, quantity, and balance is tracing the stream to reach the source.
translations.idiomatic: later scholars who establish pitch from measure, quantity, and weight trace the stream back to the source.

sentences.zh: 光、鎮爭論往復，前後三十年不決，大概言以律起度，以度起律之不同。

translations.literal: Guang and Zhen argued back and forth, unresolved for thirty years before and after—generally speaking of the difference between establishing measure from pitch standards and establishing pitch standards from measure.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang and Fan Zhen debated back and forth for thirty years without resolution—the dispute centered on whether measure arises from pitch or pitch from measure.

sentences.zh: 鎮深辟光以度起律之說，不知後世舍去度數，安得如古聖人默符聲氣之驗，自然而成律也哉？

translations.literal: Zhen deeply refuted Guang's theory of establishing pitch standards from measure, not knowing that if later generations abandon numerical measures, how could they attain the ancient sages' silent verification matching sound and qi, naturally completing pitch standards?
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen fiercely rejected Sima Guang's theory of pitch-from-measure, unaware that without numerical measures, later generations could never achieve the ancient sages' silent verification of sound and qi, by which pitch arose naturally.

sentences.zh: 至若庶之增益《漢志》八字以為脫誤，及其他紛紛之議，皆穿鑿以為新奇，雖鎮力主之，非至當之論有補於律法者也。

translations.literal: As for Fang's adding eight characters to the Han Treatises as supposed omissions, and other diverse disputes—all forced novelty; though Zhen strongly upheld them, they are not the most proper theories benefiting pitch law.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shu's addition of eight characters to the Han Treatises as supposed omissions, and other disputed points, are forced novelties. Though Fan Zhen championed them, they are not sound contributions to pitch theory.

sentences.zh: 如篪書曰《樂本》，曰《樂章》。

translations.literal: As Ruchi's book has Origins of Music and Chapters of Music.
translations.idiomatic: Ruchi's book includes Origins of Music and Chapters of Music.

sentences.zh: 沙隨程迥著《三器圖議》，曰：「體有長短，所以起度也；

translations.literal: Cheng Jiong of Shasui wrote Illustrated Discourse on the Three Instruments, saying: "Bodies have long and short—thereby measure is established;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jiong of Shasui wrote Illustrated Discourse on the Three Instruments, stating: "Bodies have length and shortness, by which measure is established;

sentences.zh: 受有多寡，所以生量也；

translations.literal: capacity has much and little—thereby quantity is generated;
translations.idiomatic: capacity has more and less, by which quantity is generated;

sentences.zh: 物有輕重，所以用權也。

translations.literal: things have light and heavy—thereby balance is employed.
translations.idiomatic: things have lightness and heaviness, by which weight is employed.

sentences.zh: 是器也，皆准之上黨羊頭山之秬黍焉。

translations.literal: These instruments all take as standard the black millet of Yangtou Mountain in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: These instruments all take as their standard the black millet of Yangtou Mountain in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 以之測幽隱之情，以之達精微之理。

translations.literal: With them one measures hidden feelings, with them one reaches subtle principles.
translations.idiomatic: With them one probes hidden truths and reaches subtle principles.

sentences.zh: 推三光之運，則不失其度；

translations.literal: Projecting the motion of the three luminaries, one does not miss their measure;
translations.idiomatic: Projecting the motions of sun, moon, and stars, one does not miss their proper measure;

sentences.zh: 通八音之變，則可召其和。

translations.literal: penetrating the transformations of the eight sounds, one can summon their harmony.
translations.idiomatic: mastering the transformations of the eight timbres, one can summon harmony.

sentences.zh: 以辨上下則有品，以分隆殺則有節。

translations.literal: To distinguish high and low there are grades; to divide prosperity and decline there are rhythms.
translations.idiomatic: To distinguish high and low there are grades; to mark prosperity and decline there are rhythms.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷之出治，生民之日用，未有頃刻不資焉者也。

translations.literal: All the court's governance and the people's daily use—there is not an instant that does not rely on them.
translations.idiomatic: Court governance and daily life alike depend on them at every moment.

sentences.zh: 古人以度定量，以量定權，必參相得，然後黃鐘之律可求，八音五聲從之而應也。

translations.literal: The ancients used measure to fix quantity, quantity to fix balance—they must mutually accord; then Yellow Bell's pitch standards can be sought, and the eight sounds and five tones respond accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients fixed quantity by measure and weight by quantity; all must align. Only then can Yellow Bell pitch be determined and the eight timbres and five tones respond in harmony.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，阮逸、胡瑗累黍定尺，既大於周尺，姑欲合其量也，然竟于權不合，乃謂黍稱二兩，已得官稱一兩，反疑史書之誤。

translations.literal: In Huangyou, Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan stacked grains to fix the foot—already larger than the Zhou foot, they wished to match quantity, yet in the end it did not accord with balance; they said two ounces of millet already equaled one official ounce, and instead suspected historical books were wrong.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan stacked millet to fix the foot measure. Though larger than the Zhou foot, they tried to match quantity—but weight still failed to align. They claimed two ounces of millet equaled one official ounce and suspected the historical records were wrong.

sentences.zh: 及韓琦、丁度詳定，知逸、瑗之失，亦莫能以三器參相考也。」

translations.literal: When Han Qi and Ding Du made detailed determinations, they knew Yi and Yuan's error, yet also could not cross-examine with the three instruments."
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi and Ding Du made a detailed review, they recognized Yi and Yuan's error, yet still could not reconcile the three instruments by cross-comparison."

sentences.zh: 先是，鎮上封事曰：「樂者，和氣也；

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhen submitted a memorial saying: "Music is harmonious qi;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fan Zhen submitted a memorial stating: "Music is harmonious qi;

sentences.zh: 發和氣者，音聲也。

translations.literal: what releases harmonious qi is sound.
translations.idiomatic: what releases harmonious qi is sound;

sentences.zh: 音聲生於無形，故古人以有形之物傳其法，俾後人參考之。

translations.literal: Sound arises from the formless; thus the ancients used formed things to transmit their method, enabling later people to consult it.
translations.idiomatic: Sound arises from the formless; the ancients therefore transmitted their method through tangible objects for later generations to consult.

sentences.zh: 有形者何？

translations.literal: What are the formed things?
translations.idiomatic: What are these tangible objects?

sentences.zh: 秬黍也、律也、尺也、龠也、鬴也、斛也、算數也、權稱也、鐘也、磬也，是十者必相合而不相戾，而後為得也。」

translations.literal: Black millet, pitch standards, foot, yue, fu, hu, counting numbers, balance and steelyard, bell, chime-stone—these ten must accord without conflict, and only then is it attained."
translations.idiomatic: Black millet, pitch pipes, the foot measure, the yue, the fu, the hu, counting rods, the balance, bells, and chime-stones—these ten must align without contradiction before the system is complete.

sentences.zh: 迥謂：「以黍定三器，則十者無不該。

translations.literal: Jiong said: "Fixing the three instruments by millet, then the ten are all covered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong replied: "Fix the three instruments by millet, and all ten are encompassed.

sentences.zh: 三者，尺為之本。

translations.literal: Of the three, the foot is the root.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three, the foot measure is fundamental.

sentences.zh: 周尺也者，先儒考其制，吻合者不一。

translations.literal: As for the Zhou foot, former Confucians examined its system—those that matched were not one.
translations.idiomatic: Former scholars examined the Zhou foot measure, but their reconstructions did not agree.

sentences.zh: 至宋祁取《隋書》大業中歷代尺十五等，獨以周尺為之本，以考諸尺。

translations.literal: When Song Qi took the Book of Sui's fifteen grades of successive-dynasty feet from the Daye era, he alone took the Zhou foot as root to examine all feet.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qi drew on the Book of Sui's fifteen grades of historical foot measures from the Daye era, taking the Zhou foot alone as the standard for comparison.

sentences.zh: 韓琦嘉祐累黍尺二，其一亦與周尺相近。

translations.literal: Han Qi's two Jiayou stacked-grain feet—one also nears the Zhou foot.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi's two Jiayou millet-stacked foot measures—one of which also approximates the Zhou foot.

sentences.zh: 司馬備刻之于石。

translations.literal: Sima had them carved on stone for preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang had them carved in stone for preservation.

sentences.zh: 光舊物也。

translations.literal: Guang's old objects.
translations.idiomatic: These were Guang's own artifacts.

sentences.zh: 苟以是定尺，又以是參定權量，以合諸器，如挈裘而振其領，其順者不可勝數也。」

translations.literal: If using this to fix the foot, and using this to cross-fix balance and quantity to harmonize all instruments—like lifting a fur coat by its collar—the accordances would be beyond counting."
translations.idiomatic: If the foot is fixed thereby, and weight and quantity cross-calibrated to harmonize all instruments—like lifting a fur coat by its collar—the resulting alignments would be beyond counting."

sentences.zh: 迥博學好古，朱熹深禮敬之。

translations.literal: Jiong was broadly learned and fond of antiquity; Zhu Xi deeply honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was erudite and devoted to antiquity; Zhu Xi treated him with deep respect.

sentences.zh: 其後江陵府學教授廬陵彭應龍，既注《漢·律曆志》，設為問答，著《鐘律辨疑》三卷，至為精密，發古人所未言者。

translations.literal: Afterward Peng Yinglong of Luling, professor at Jiangling Prefecture School, having annotated the Han Treatises on Pitch Standards and Calendar, set up questions and answers, and wrote three volumes of Discerning Doubts on Bell Pitch Standards—extremely precise, expressing what the ancients had not spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Later Peng Yinglong of Luling, a professor at the Jiangling prefectural school, annotated the Han Treatises on Pitch Standards and Calendar, composed a question-and-answer treatise, and wrote three volumes of Discerning Doubts on Bell Pitch Standards—remarkably precise, articulating points the ancients had never addressed.

sentences.zh: 宋曆在東都凡八改，曰《應天》、《乾元》、《儀天》、《崇天》、《明天》、《奉元》、《觀天》、《紀元》。

translations.literal: Song calendars at the Eastern Capital were changed eight times in all: Responding to Heaven, Qianyuan, Yitian, Chongtian, Mingtian, Fengyuan, Guantian, and Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital the Song revised its calendar eight times: Responding to Heaven, Qianyuan, Yitian, Chongtian, Mingtian, Fengyuan, Guantian, and Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 星翁離散，《紀元曆》亡，紹興二年，高宗重購得之，六月甲午，語輔臣曰：「曆官推步不精，今曆差一日，近得《紀元曆》，自明年當改正，協時月正日，蓋非細事。」

translations.literal: Star chroniclers scattered, and the Jiyuan Calendar was lost. In the second year of Shaoxing, Emperor Gaozong heavily purchased and obtained it. On the jiawu day of the sixth month he told his chief ministers: "The calendar officials' computations are not precise; today the calendar is off by one day. I have recently obtained the Jiyuan Calendar; from next year it should be corrected, harmonizing seasons, months, and the correct day—this is no minor matter."
translations.idiomatic: Star chroniclers had scattered, and the Jiyuan Calendar was lost. In Shaoxing year 2, Emperor Gaozong paid heavily to recover it. On the sixth month's jiawu day he told his ministers: "The calendar officials' computations are imprecise—the calendar is now one day off. I have recovered the Jiyuan Calendar; from next year it will be corrected to harmonize seasons, months, and the correct day. This is no small matter."

sentences.zh: 是歲，始議制渾儀。

translations.literal: That year they first discussed making a armillary sphere.
translations.idiomatic: That year they first discussed constructing an armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 十一月，工部言，《渾儀法要》當以子午為正，今欲定測樞極，合差局官二員。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Ministry of Works said: Essentials of the Armillary Sphere Method should take the meridian as correct; now wishing to fix measurement of the pivot pole, two officials of the Astrological Bureau should be appointed.
