translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Ministry of Works reported that the Essentials of the Armillary Sphere Method requires the meridian as reference; to fix measurement of the celestial pole, two Astrological Bureau officials should be appointed.

sentences.zh: 詔差李繼宗等充測驗定正宮，俟造畢進呈日，同參詳指說制度官丁師仁、李公謹入殿安設。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Li Jizong and others to fill posts testing and correcting the palace; when construction was finished and presented, on the day of presentation Ding Shiren and Li Gongjin, officials explaining the system, would enter the hall to install it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Li Jizong and others to test and correct the instrument; when finished, Ding Shiren and Li Gongjin, officials responsible for explaining the design, would install it in the hall.

sentences.zh: 三年正月壬戌，進呈渾儀木樣。

translations.literal: In the third year, first month, renxu day, the wooden model of the armillary sphere was presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, first month, day renxu, the wooden model of the armillary sphere was presented.

sentences.zh: 壬申，太史局令丁師仁等言，省識東都渾儀四座：在測驗渾儀刻漏所曰至道儀，在翰林天文局曰皇祐儀，在太史局天文院曰熙寧儀，在合台曰元祐儀，每座約銅二萬餘斤，今若半之，當萬餘斤。

translations.literal: On renshen day, Astrological Bureau Director Ding Shiren and others said they recognized four armillary spheres of the Eastern Capital: at the Testing Armillary Sphere and Clepsydra Office, called the Zhidao Instrument; at the Hanlin Astrological Bureau, called the Huangyou Instrument; at the Astrological Bureau Astronomy Court, called the Xining Instrument; at the Secretariat, called the Yuanyou Instrument—each about more than twenty thousand jin of copper; if halved now, it should be more than ten thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: On day renshen, Astrological Bureau Director Ding Shiren reported four Eastern Capital armillary spheres: the Zhidao Instrument at the Testing Office; the Huangyou Instrument at the Hanlin Bureau; the Xining Instrument at the Astronomy Court; and the Yuanyou Instrument at the Secretariat—each requiring over 20,000 jin of copper; half that would be over 10,000 jin.

sentences.zh: 且元祐製造，有兩府提舉。

translations.literal: Moreover the Yuanyou manufacture had the two departments supervise.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanyou manufacture had been supervised by both metropolitan offices.

sentences.zh: 時都司覆實，用銅八千四百斤。

translations.literal: At that time the Capital Bureau verified actual use: eight thousand four hundred jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Bureau verified actual usage at 8,400 jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 詔工部置物料，臨安府傭工匠，仍令工部長、貳提舉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Works to prepare materials, Lin'an Prefecture to hire craftsmen, and still ordered the Ministry director and deputy to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of Works to prepare materials, Lin'an Prefecture to hire craftsmen, and the ministry director and deputy to supervise.

sentences.zh: 五年，日官言，正月朔旦日食九分半，虧在辰正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year calendar officials said: on the first day of the first month the sun would be eclipsed nine and a half tenths, with obscuration at chen zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 calendar officials predicted a solar eclipse of nine-tenths on the first day of the first month, with obscuration at the fifth double-hour of chen.

sentences.zh: 常州布衣陳得一言：當食八分半，虧在巳初。

translations.literal: Chen Deyi, commoner of Changzhou, said: the eclipse should be eight and a half tenths, with obscuration at the beginning of si.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deyi, a commoner of Changzhou, predicted an eight-tenths eclipse with obscuration at the beginning of si.

sentences.zh: 其言卒驗。

translations.literal: His words in the end were verified.
translations.idiomatic: His prediction proved correct.

sentences.zh: 侍御史張致遠言：「今歲正月朔日食，太史所定不驗，得一嘗為臣言，皆有依據。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Censor Zhang Zhiyuan said: "This year's first-month new-moon solar eclipse—the Astrological Bureau's determination was not verified; Deyi once told your servant, all with basis.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Zhiyuan memorialized: "This year's new-moon eclipse was mispredicted by the Astrological Bureau, yet Deyi had told me his prediction with sound basis.

sentences.zh: 蓋患算造者不能通消息、盈虛之奧，進退、遲疾之分，致立朔有訛。

translations.literal: The trouble is that computational makers cannot penetrate the mysteries of communication, fullness and emptiness, advance and retreat, slow and fast distinctions, causing errors in fixing the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The problem is that calendar makers fail to grasp the mysteries of syzygy, lunar phases, and planetary motion, leading to errors in fixing the new moon.

sentences.zh: 凡定朔小餘七千五百以上者，進一日。

translations.literal: Whenever fixing the new moon, if the small remainder is seven thousand five hundred or above, advance one day.
translations.idiomatic: When the fractional remainder for the new moon reaches 7,500 or above, one day must be advanced.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年十二月小餘七千六百八十，太史不進，故十一月小盡；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Shaoxing year 4 the small remainder was seven thousand six hundred eighty—the Astrological Bureau did not advance, so the eleventh month had a short end;
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing the fourth year, month 12, the small remainder was 7,680—the bureau failed to advance, so month 11 ended short;

sentences.zh: 今年五月小餘七千一百八十，少三百二十，乃為進朔，四月大盡。

translations.literal: this year in the fifth month the small remainder was seven thousand one hundred eighty—three hundred twenty less—and thus became an advanced new moon; the fourth month had a long end.
translations.idiomatic: this year in month 5 the remainder was 7,180—320 less—triggering an advanced new moon; month 4 ended long.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年定十一月三十日甲戌為臘，陰陽書曰：臘者，接也，以故接新，在十二月近大寒前後戌日定之，若近大寒戌日在正月十一日，若即用遠大寒戌日定之，庶不出十二月。

translations.literal: In Jianyan year 3 they fixed the thirtieth day of the eleventh month, jiaxu, as La; yin-yang books say: La means connecting, connecting old with new, fixed on a xu day near Great Cold in the twelfth month; if the xu day near Great Cold falls on the eleventh day of the first month, then use the xu day farther from Great Cold to fix it, so it does not fall outside the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan year 3 they fixed day jiaxu of month 11, day 30, as La. Yin-yang texts state that La means "connecting" old and new, fixed on a xu day near Great Cold in month 12; if that xu day falls in month 1, the more distant xu day is used so La never falls outside month 12.

sentences.zh: 如宣和五年十二月二十七日丙午大寒，後四日庚戌，雖近，緣在六年正月一日，此時以十九日戊戌為臘。

translations.literal: As in Xuanhe year 5, the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, bingwu, was Great Cold; four days later was gengxu—though near, because it fell on the first day of the sixth year, at that time they took the nineteenth day, wuxu, as La.
translations.idiomatic: For example, in Xuanhe year 5, day bingwu of month 12, day 27, was Great Cold; four days later was gengxu—though near, it fell on day 1 of year 6, so day wuxu of day 19 was taken as La.

sentences.zh: 得一於歲旦日食，嘗預言之，不差厘刻。

translations.literal: Deyi, on the new-year-day solar eclipse, once predicted it in advance, not off by a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi had predicted the new-year solar eclipse in advance, accurate to the finest measure.

sentences.zh: 願詔得一改造新曆，委官專董其事。

translations.literal: I wish an edict ordering Deyi to remake a new calendar, appointing officials specifically to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: I request an edict commissioning Deyi to create a new calendar under dedicated official supervision.

sentences.zh: 仍盡取其書，參校太史有無，以補遺闕。

translations.literal: Still take all his books completely, collate with what the Astrological Bureau has or lacks, to supplement omissions.
translations.idiomatic: His complete works should be collected and collated against the bureau's holdings to fill gaps.

sentences.zh: 擇曆算子弟粗通了者，授演撰之要，庶幾日官無曠，曆法不絕。」

translations.literal: Select calendar-computing youths with rough understanding and teach them essentials of compilation, so that perhaps calendar officials will not be vacant and calendar methods will not cease."
translations.idiomatic: Select youths with basic calendar skills and teach them computation, so the bureau is never understaffed and methods are not lost."

sentences.zh: 二月丙子，詔秘書少監朱震即秘書省監視得一改造新曆。

translations.literal: On the second month, bingzi day, an edict ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhu Zhen to supervise at the Secretariat Deyi's remaking of the new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: On month 2, day bingzi, an edict ordered Vice Director Zhu Zhen to supervise Deyi's calendar work at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 八月，曆成，震請賜名《統元》，從之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the calendar was completed; Zhen requested the name Unifying Origin, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In month 8 the calendar was finished; Zhen requested the name Unifying Origin, which was approved.

sentences.zh: 詔翰林學士孫近為序，以六年頒行，遷震一秩，賜得一通微處士，官其一子。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Academician Sun Jin to write the preface; it was promulgated in the sixth year; Zhen was promoted one rank; Deyi was granted the title Erudite Recluse of Penetrating Subtlety, and one son was given office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commissioned Academician Sun Jin to write the preface; promulgated in year 6; Zhen was promoted; Deyi received the title Erudite Recluse of Penetrating Subtlety and an office for his son.

sentences.zh: 道士裴伯壽等受賞有差。

translations.literal: Daoist Pei Boshou and others received rewards in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Pei Boshou and others received graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 得一等上推甲子之歲，得十一月甲子朔夜半冬至日度起於虛中以為元。

translations.literal: Deyi and others pushed back to the jiazi year, obtaining the eleventh month's jiazi new moon at midnight winter solstice, sun's position starting from Emptiness as the origin.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi and colleagues traced back to the jiazi year, finding the jiazi new moon of month 11 at midnight winter solstice, with the sun's position at Emptiness as the epoch.

sentences.zh: 著《歷經》七卷，《曆議》二卷，《立成》四卷，《考古春秋日食》一卷，《七曜細行》二卷，《氣朔入行草》一卷，詔付太史氏，副藏秘府。

translations.literal: He wrote seven volumes of Calendar Classic, two of Calendar Discourse, four of Establishment Tables, one of Investigating Ancient Spring and Autumn Solar Eclipses, two of Detailed Motion of the Seven Luminaries, one of Draft of Qi, New Moon, and Planetary Entry—issued an edict to the Astrological Bureau with a copy stored in the secret repository.
translations.idiomatic: He produced seven volumes of Calendar Classic, two of Calendar Discourse, four of Establishment Tables, one on ancient solar eclipses, two on the seven luminaries, and one draft on qi and new moons—deposited with the Astrological Bureau and the secret repository.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，史官重修神宗正史，求《奉元曆》不獲，詔陳得一、裴伯壽赴闕補修之。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing year 9, when historiographers revised Emperor Shenzong's standard history, they sought the Fengyuan Calendar but could not obtain it; an edict ordered Chen Deyi and Pei Boshou to come to court to supplement and revise it.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year 9, revising Shenzong's standard history, historians could not find the Fengyuan Calendar; Chen Deyi and Pei Boshou were summoned to restore it.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太史局請制渾儀，工部員外郎謝伋言：「臣嘗詢渾儀之法，太史官生論議不同，鑄作之工，今尚闕焉。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Astrological Bureau requested making an armillary sphere; Ministry of Works Outer Gentleman Xie Ji said: "Your servant once inquired into armillary sphere methods; Astrological Bureau students discuss differently, and casting craftsmen are still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 the Astrological Bureau requested an armillary sphere; Xie Ji of the Ministry of Works reported: "I have inquired into armillary methods, but bureau students disagree and skilled casters are lacking.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜先詢訪制度，敷求通曉天文歷數之學者，參訂是非，斯合古制。」

translations.literal: Your servant thinks one should first inquire into the system, widely seek those versed in astronomy and calendar numbers, jointly determine right and wrong—then it will accord with ancient system."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed first establishing the design, consulting experts in astronomy and calendrics, and reconciling disputes to match ancient standards."

sentences.zh: 蘇頌之子應詔赴闕，請訪求其父遺書，考質制度。

translations.literal: Su Song's son Yingcan came to court, requesting to seek his father's surviving books and examine the system.
translations.idiomatic: Su Song's son Yingcan came to court seeking his father's surviving texts to verify the design.

sentences.zh: 宰相秦檜曰：「在廷之臣，罕能通曉。」

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Qin Hui said: "Among court ministers, few can thoroughly understand."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Qin Hui said: "Few court ministers understand these matters thoroughly."

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「此闕典也，朕已就宮中製造，範制雖小，可用窺測，日以晷度、夜以樞星為則，非久降出，第當廣其尺寸爾。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "This is a missing classic; I have already had it made in the palace—the model though small can be used for observation; by day use the gnomon shadow, by night use the pivot stars as standard—not long before it descends; only its dimensions should be enlarged."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong replied: "This classic is missing; I have already had a model made in the palace—small but usable for observation by day via the gnomon and by night via the pole star. It will soon be issued; only its size need be enlarged."

sentences.zh: 於是命檜提舉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Hui to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Hui to supervise.

sentences.zh: 時內侍邵諤善運思，專令主之，累年方成。

translations.literal: At that time inner attendant Shao E was skilled in deliberation and was specially put in charge; after many years it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Shao E, skilled in design, was put in charge; completion took many years.

sentences.zh: 《統元曆》頒行雖久，有司不善用之，暗用《紀元》法推步，而以《統元》為名。

translations.literal: Though the Unifying Origin Calendar had long been promulgated, officials did not know how to use it well, secretly using Jiyuan methods for computation while naming it Unifying Origin.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Unifying Origin Calendar had long been in use, officials poorly applied it, secretly computing by Jiyuan methods while retaining the Unifying Origin name.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年，日官以《紀元曆》推三年丁亥歲十一月甲子朔，將頒行，裴伯壽詣禮部陳《統元曆》法當進作乙丑朔，於是依《統元曆》法正之。

translations.literal: In Qiandao year 2 calendar officials using the Jiyuan Calendar computed the dinghai year 3 eleventh month's jiazi new moon for promulgation; Pei Boshou went to the Ministry of Rites stating Unifying Origin methods should advance to yichou new moon—thereupon they corrected according to Unifying Origin methods.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao year 2, using Jiyuan methods, officials computed the jiazi new moon of month 11, dinghai year 3, for promulgation; Pei Boshou argued Unifying Origin required yichou new moon, and correction followed.

sentences.zh: 光州士人劉孝榮言：「《統元曆》交食先天六刻，火星差天二度。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaorong, scholar of Guang Prefecture, said: "The Unifying Origin Calendar's eclipses are six quarters too early, Mars two degrees off in the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar Liu Xiaorong of Guang Prefecture said the Unifying Origin Calendar predicted eclipses six quarters too early and Mars two degrees off.

sentences.zh: 嘗自著曆，期以半年可成，願改造新曆。」

translations.literal: He once composed a calendar himself, expecting to finish in half a year, wishing to remake a new calendar."
translations.idiomatic: He had composed his own calendar, expecting completion in six months, and sought to create a new one.

sentences.zh: 禮部謂：「《統元曆》法用之十有五年，《紀元曆》法經六十年，日月交食有先天分數之差，五星細行亦有二三度分之殊。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "Unifying Origin methods have been used fifteen years; Jiyuan methods for sixty years—solar and lunar eclipses have early-by-fraction differences; the five planets' detailed motion also differ two or three degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites noted that Unifying Origin had been used fifteen years and Jiyuan sixty; eclipses showed fractional error and the five planets differed by two or three degrees.

sentences.zh: 算造曆官拘于依經用法，致朔日有進退，氣節日分有誤，于時宜改造。」

translations.literal: Calendar-making officials, constrained by following canonical usage, caused new-moon advance and retreat and solar-term day-fraction errors—at the time a remake was appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Officials bound to canonical methods caused new-moon and solar-term errors—a remake was timely.

sentences.zh: 伯壽言：「造曆必先立表測景驗氣，庶幾精密。」

translations.literal: Boshou said: "Making a calendar must first set up tables and measure shadows to verify qi—then one can be precise."
translations.idiomatic: Boshou said a new calendar requires gnomon measurements to verify qi before precision is possible.

sentences.zh: 判太史局吳澤私于孝榮，且言銅表難成、木表易壞以沮之。

translations.literal: Astrological Bureau judge Wu Ze privately favored Xiaorong, and said copper tables are hard to make and wood tables easy to ruin to obstruct this.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau judge Wu Ze favored Xiaorong privately and claimed copper gnomons were impractical and wooden ones perishable.

sentences.zh: 乃詔禮部尚書周執羔提領改造新曆，執羔亦謂測景驗氣，經涉歲月。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Rites Zhou Zhigao to supervise remaking the new calendar; Zhigao also said measuring shadows and verifying qi would take months.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Zhigao was ordered to supervise; he too said gnomon testing would take months.

sentences.zh: 孝榮乃采萬分曆，作三萬分以為日法，號《七曜細行曆》，上之。

translations.literal: Xiaorong then adopted the myriad-part calendar, making thirty thousand parts as day method, titled Detailed Motion of the Seven Luminaries Calendar, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaorong adopted a myriad-part system, using thirty thousand as the day divisor, titled Detailed Motion of the Seven Luminaries Calendar, and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 三年，執羔以歷來上，孝宗曰：「日月有盈縮，須隨時修改。」

translations.literal: In the third year Zhigao submitted the calendar; Emperor Xiaozong said: "Sun and moon have waxing and waning—one must modify according to the time."
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Zhigao submitted the calendar; Xiaozong said sun and moon vary and must be adjusted in season.

sentences.zh: 執羔對曰：「舜協時月正日，正為積久不能無差，故協正之。」

translations.literal: Zhigao replied: "Shun harmonized seasons, months, and the correct day—correcting because long accumulation cannot be without difference, hence harmonizing and correcting."
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao replied that Shun harmonized seasons and the correct day because accumulated error requires periodic correction.

sentences.zh: 孝宗問曰：「今曆與古曆何如？」

translations.literal: Xiaozong asked: "How is today's calendar compared with the ancient calendar?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong asked how the new calendar compared with antiquity.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「堯時冬至日在牽牛，今冬至日在鬥一度。」

translations.literal: He replied: "At Yao's time winter solstice sun was in Ox; today winter solstice sun is in Dipper one degree."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "At Yao's time winter solstice fell in Ox; today it falls at Dipper, one degree."

sentences.zh: 孝榮《七曜細行曆》自謂精密，且預定是年四月戊辰朔日食一分，日官言食二分，伯壽並非之，既而精明不食。

translations.literal: Xiaorong's Detailed Motion Calendar claimed precision and predetermined that year's fourth month, wuchen new moon, solar eclipse one tenth; calendar officials said two tenths; Boshou rejected both—in the end it was bright and did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaorong's calendar claimed precision and predicted a one-tenth eclipse on the wuchen new moon of month 4; officials said two-tenths; Boshou rejected both—the eclipse did not occur.

sentences.zh: 孝榮又定八月庚戌望月食六分半，候之，止及五分。

translations.literal: Xiaorong also fixed the eighth month, gengxu full moon, lunar eclipse six and a half tenths; observing it, only reached five tenths.
translations.idiomatic: He predicted a six-tenths lunar eclipse on the gengxu full moon of month 8; observation showed only five-tenths.

sentences.zh: 又定戊子歲二月丁未望月食九分以上，出地，其光復滿。

translations.literal: He also fixed the wuzi year second month, dingwei full moon, lunar eclipse more than nine tenths, emerging from earth with light fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: He predicted a lunar eclipse over nine-tenths on the dingwei full moon of month 2, wuzi year, with the moon emerging and light restored.

sentences.zh: 伯壽言：「當食既，復滿在戌正三刻。」

translations.literal: Boshou said: "It should be total eclipse, full restoration at the third quarter of xu zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Boshou said it should be total, with full restoration at the third quarter of the xu period.

sentences.zh: 侍御史單時言：「比年太史局以《統元曆》稍差而用《紀元曆》，《紀元》浸差，邇者劉孝榮議改曆，四月朔日食不驗，日官兩用《統元》、《紀元》以定晦朔，二曆之差，歲益已甚，非所以明天道、正人事也。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Censor Shan Shi said: "In recent years the Astrological Bureau, because Unifying Origin is slightly off, uses Jiyuan Calendar; Jiyuan gradually errs; lately Liu Xiaorong discussed remaking the calendar—the fourth-month new-moon eclipse was not verified; calendar officials use both Unifying Origin and Jiyuan to fix last days of months—the two calendars' difference yearly grows worse—not the way to clarify heaven's way and correct human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shan Shi memorialized that the bureau, finding Unifying Origin slightly off, used Jiyuan, which also drifted; Xiaorong's new calendar failed the month-4 eclipse test; using both calendars worsened discrepancy yearly—this failed to clarify heaven's way.

sentences.zh: 如四月朔之日不食，雖為差誤，然一分之說，猶為近焉。

translations.literal: As on the fourth-month new-moon day there was no eclipse—though an error, the one-tenth prediction was still relatively near.
translations.idiomatic: Though month 4's eclipse failed, the one-tenth prediction was relatively close.

sentences.zh: 八月望之月食五分，新曆以為食六分，亦為近焉。

translations.literal: The eighth-month full-moon eclipse was five tenths; the new calendar said six tenths—also relatively near.
translations.idiomatic: The month-8 full-moon eclipse was five-tenths; the new calendar predicted six—also relatively close.

sentences.zh: 聞欲以明年二月望月食為驗，是夜或有陰晦風雨，願令日官與孝榮所定七政躔度其說異同者，俟其可驗之時，以渾象測之，察其稍近而屢中者，從其說以定曆，庶幾不致甚差。」

translations.literal: I hear they wish to use next year's second-month full-moon eclipse as verification—that night may have cloud, wind, or rain; I wish calendar officials and Xiaorong's differing computations for the seven regulators be compared when verifiable, tested with the armillary sphere, and whichever is nearer and often hits be adopted to fix the calendar, so error is not great."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed comparing Xiaorong's and official predictions at the next verifiable eclipse, using the armillary sphere, and adopting whichever proves more accurate.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔國子司業權禮部侍郎程大昌、監察御史張敦實監太史局驗之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict ordered Guozi Vice Director acting Minister of Rites Cheng Dachang and Investigating Censor Zhang Dunshi to supervise the Astrological Bureau's verification.
translations.idiomatic: In month 11 Cheng Dachang and Zhang Dunshi were ordered to supervise bureau testing.

sentences.zh: 時孝宗務知曆法疏密，詔太史局以高宗所降小渾儀測驗造曆。

translations.literal: At that time Xiaozong wished to know calendar methods' density and sparsity; he issued an edict the bureau to use Gaozong's descended small armillary sphere to test and make calendars.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong, seeking to judge calendrical precision, ordered testing with Gaozong's small armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 四年二月十四日丁未望，月食生光復滿，如伯壽言。

translations.literal: On the fourth year second month fourteenth day, dingwei full moon, lunar eclipse light fully restored—as Boshou said.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth year, month 2, day 14, dingwei full moon, the eclipse restored fully—as Boshou predicted.

sentences.zh: 時等又言：「去年承詔，十二月癸卯、乙巳兩夜監測太陰、太白，新曆為近。

translations.literal: Shi and others also said: "Last year receiving the edict, on the nights of the twelfth month's guimao and yisi we monitored the moon and Venus—the new calendar was nearer.
translations.idiomatic: Shi reported that on guimao and yisi nights of month 12 the previous year, the new calendar matched the moon and Venus better.

sentences.zh: 今年二月十四日望月食，臣與大昌等以渾儀定其光滿，則舊曆差近，新曆差遠。

translations.literal: This year's second-month fourteenth full-moon eclipse—we and Dachang fixed full restoration with the armillary sphere; then the old calendar was slightly nearer, the new farther.
translations.idiomatic: For this year's month-2 day-14 eclipse, they found the old calendar slightly nearer for full restoration.

sentences.zh: 若遽以舊曆為是，則去年所測四事皆新曆為近，今者所定月食，乃復稍差，以是知天道之難測。

translations.literal: If we abruptly take the old calendar as correct, then last year's four tests all favored the new calendar; now this full-moon fixation is again slightly off—thus one knows heaven's way is hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: He noted inconsistency: last year favored the new calendar; this eclipse favored the old—heaven's way is hard to measure.

sentences.zh: 儒者莫肯究心，一付之星翁曆家，其說又不精密。

translations.literal: Confucians are unwilling to investigate thoroughly, leaving it all to star chroniclers and calendar families whose theories are also not precise.
translations.idiomatic: Confucians neglect the matter, leaving it to star chroniclers whose theories lack precision.

sentences.zh: 願令繼宗、孝榮等更定三月一日內七政躔度之異同者，仍令臣等往視測驗而造曆焉。」

translations.literal: I wish Jizong, Xiaorong, and others further fix differences in the seven regulators' positions within the third month first day, and still order us to go observe, test, and make the calendar."
translations.idiomatic: He requested Jizong and Xiaorong to reconcile planetary positions by month 3 day 1 and authorize further observation.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔時與大昌同驗之。

translations.literal: In the third month an edict ordered Shi and Dachang together to verify.
translations.idiomatic: In month 3 Shi and Dachang were ordered to verify together.

sentences.zh: 太史局止用《紀元曆》與新曆測驗，未嘗參以《統元曆》。

translations.literal: The Astrological Bureau only used Jiyuan Calendar and the new calendar for testing, never participating Unifying Origin Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau tested only Jiyuan and the new calendar, not Unifying Origin.

sentences.zh: 臣等先求判太史局李繼宗、天文官劉孝榮等《統元》、《紀元》、新曆異同，於三月初九日夜、十一日早、十四日夜、二十日早詣太史局，召三曆官上臺，用銅儀窺管對測太陰、木、火、土星昏晨度經歷度數，參稽所供，監視測驗。

translations.literal: Your servants first sought Astrological Bureau judge Li Jizong, astronomy officer Liu Xiaorong, and others' differences among Unifying Origin, Jiyuan, and new calendars; on the third month ninth night, eleventh morning, fourteenth night, and twentieth morning we went to the bureau, summoned three calendar officers to the platform, used the bronze instrument's sighting tube to measure the moon, wood star, fire star, and earth star's dusk and dawn degrees and traversed degrees, collating supplied materials and supervising tests.
translations.idiomatic: They compared all three calendars on nights of month 3 days 9, 11, 14, and 20 using the bronze armillary sighting tube.

sentences.zh: 初九日昏度：舊曆太陰在黃道張宿十二度八十七分，在赤道張宿十度；

translations.literal: Ninth night dusk degree: old calendar moon on ecliptic Extended thirteen degrees eighty-seven parts, on equator Extended ten degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Night of day 9 dusk: old calendar placed the moon at Extended 13°87' ecliptic, 10° equator;

sentences.zh: 新曆在黃道張宿十四度四十分，在赤道張宿十五度太。

translations.literal: new calendar on ecliptic Extended fourteen degrees forty parts, on equator Extended fifteen degrees great.
translations.idiomatic: new calendar at Extended 14°40' ecliptic, 15°+ equator.

sentences.zh: 臣等驗得在赤道張宿十五度半。

translations.literal: Your servants verified it at equator Extended fifteen degrees half.
translations.idiomatic: Verification showed equator Extended 15.5°.

sentences.zh: 今考之新曆稍密，舊曆皆疏。

translations.literal: Examining now, the new calendar is slightly dense; old calendars are all sparse.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar proved slightly more accurate; old calendars were loose.

sentences.zh: 十一日早晨度：木星在黃道室宿十五度七分，在赤道室宿十三度少；

translations.literal: Eleventh morning degree: wood star on ecliptic Encampments fifteen degrees seven parts, on equator Encampments thirteen degrees little;
translations.idiomatic: Morning of day 11: Jupiter at Encampments 15°7' ecliptic, 13°− equator;

sentences.zh: 土星在黃道虛宿七度三分，在赤道虛宿七度強。

translations.literal: earth star on ecliptic Emptiness seven degrees three parts, on equator Emptiness seven degrees strong.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn at Emptiness 7°3' ecliptic, 7°+ equator.

sentences.zh: 新曆木星在黃道室宿十五度四十四分，在赤道室宿十四度少弱；

translations.literal: New calendar wood star on ecliptic Encampments fifteen degrees forty-four parts, on equator Encampments fourteen degrees little weak;
translations.idiomatic: New calendar: Jupiter Encampments 15°44' ecliptic, 14°− equator;

sentences.zh: 土星在黃道虛宿六度二十一分，在赤道虛宿六度少弱。

translations.literal: earth star on ecliptic Emptiness six degrees twenty-one parts, on equator Emptiness six degrees little weak.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn Emptiness 6°21' ecliptic, 6°− equator.

sentences.zh: 臣等驗得五更三點，土星在赤道虛宿六度弱；

translations.literal: Your servants verified at fifth watch third point earth star at equator Emptiness six degrees weak;
translations.idiomatic: At fifth watch, third point: Saturn equator Emptiness 6°−;

sentences.zh: 五更五點，木星在赤道室宿十四度。

translations.literal: fifth watch fifth point wood star at equator Encampments fourteen degrees.
translations.idiomatic: fifth watch, fifth point: Jupiter equator Encampments 14°.

sentences.zh: 今考之新曆稍密，舊曆皆疏。

translations.literal: Examining now, the new calendar is slightly dense; old calendars are all sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Again the new calendar was denser; old calendars sparse.

sentences.zh: 十二日，都省令定驗《統元》、《紀元》及新曆疏密。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day the Secretariat ordered fixing density and sparsity of Unifying Origin, Jiyuan, and new calendars.
translations.idiomatic: On day 12 the Secretariat ordered final comparison of all three calendars.

sentences.zh: 《統元曆》昏度，太陰在黃道氐宿初度九十四分，在赤道氐宿三度少；

translations.literal: Unifying Origin Calendar dusk degree, moon on ecliptic Base one degree ninety-four parts, on equator Base three degrees little;
translations.idiomatic: Unifying Origin dusk: moon Base 1°94' ecliptic, 3°− equator;

sentences.zh: 《紀元曆》在黃道氐宿初度八十三分，在赤道氐宿二度太；

translations.literal: Jiyuan Calendar on ecliptic Base one degree eighty-three parts, on equator Base two degrees great;
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan: Base 1°83' ecliptic, 2°+ equator;

sentences.zh: 新曆在黃道亢宿八度七十一分，在赤道亢宿九度少弱。

translations.literal: new calendar on ecliptic Horn eight degrees seventy-one parts, on equator Horn nine degrees little weak.
translations.idiomatic: new: Horn 8°71' ecliptic, 9°− equator.

sentences.zh: 三曆官以渾儀由南數之，其太陰北去角宿距星二十一度少弱。

translations.literal: Three calendar officers counting south with the armillary sphere, the moon north from Horn distance star twenty-one degrees little weak.
translations.idiomatic: Officers measured the moon 21°− north of Horn's distance star.

sentences.zh: 新舊曆官稱昏度亢宿未見，祗以窺管測定角宿距星，復以曆書考東方七宿，角占十二度，亢占九度少；

translations.literal: New and old calendar officers said dusk degree Horn was not seen, only used the sighting tube to fix Horn distance star, then examined eastern seven lodges in calendar books—Horn occupies twelve degrees, Horn neighbor nine degrees little;
translations.idiomatic: Horn was not visible; officers measured Horn's distance star and deduced from lodge widths—

sentences.zh: 既亢宿未見，當除角宿十二度，即太陰此時在赤道亢宿九度少弱。

translations.literal: since Horn neighbor was not seen, subtract Horn's twelve degrees—then the moon at this time was on equator Horn neighbor nine degrees little weak.
translations.idiomatic: subtracting Horn's 12° placed the moon at Horn neighbor 9°− equator.

sentences.zh: 今考之新曆全密，《紀元》、《統元曆》皆疏。

translations.literal: Examining now, the new calendar is fully dense; Jiyuan and Unifying Origin calendars are all sparse.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar was fully accurate; Jiyuan and Unifying Origin were loose.

sentences.zh: 二十日早晨度：《統元曆》太陰在黃道鬥宿十一度九十一份，在赤道鬥宿十二度少；

translations.literal: Twentieth morning degree: Unifying Origin Calendar moon on ecliptic Dipper eleven degrees ninety-one parts, on equator Dipper twelve degrees little;
translations.idiomatic: Morning day 20 Unifying Origin: moon Dipper 11°91' ecliptic, 12°− equator;

sentences.zh: 火星在黃道危宿七度九十一分，在赤道危宿七度少；

translations.literal: fire star on ecliptic Rooftop seven degrees ninety-one parts, on equator Rooftop seven degrees little;
translations.idiomatic: Mars Rooftop 7°91' ecliptic, 7°− equator;

sentences.zh: 土星在黃道虛宿八度八十二分，在赤道虛宿八度太強。

translations.literal: earth star on ecliptic Emptiness eight degrees eighty-two parts, on equator Emptiness eight degrees great strong.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn Emptiness 8°82' ecliptic, 8°++ equator.

sentences.zh: 《紀元曆》太陰在黃道鬥宿十一度四十分，在赤道鬥宿十一度半；

translations.literal: Jiyuan Calendar moon on ecliptic Dipper eleven degrees forty parts, on equator Dipper eleven degrees half;
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan: moon Dipper 11°40' ecliptic, 11.5° equator;

sentences.zh: 火星在黃道危宿六度，在赤道危宿六度太；

translations.literal: fire star on ecliptic Rooftop six degrees, on equator Rooftop six degrees great;
translations.idiomatic: Mars Rooftop 6° ecliptic, 6°+ equator;

sentences.zh: 土星在黃道虛宿七度三十九分，在赤道虛宿七度半弱。

translations.literal: earth star on ecliptic Emptiness seven degrees thirty-nine parts, on equator Emptiness seven degrees half weak.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn Emptiness 7°39' ecliptic, 7.5°− equator.

sentences.zh: 新曆太陰在黃道鬥宿十度六十一分，在赤道鬥宿十度少；

translations.literal: New calendar moon on ecliptic Dipper ten degrees sixty-one parts, on equator Dipper ten degrees little;
translations.idiomatic: New calendar: moon Dipper 10°61' ecliptic, 10°− equator;

sentences.zh: 火星在黃道危宿七度二十分，在赤道危宿六度；

translations.literal: Mars on ecliptic Rooftop seven degrees twenty parts, on equator Rooftop six degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Mars at Rooftop 7°20' ecliptic, 6° equator;

sentences.zh: 土星在黃道虛宿六度五十三分，在赤道虛宿六度半。

translations.literal: Saturn on ecliptic Emptiness six degrees fifty-three parts, on equator Emptiness six degrees half.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn at Emptiness 6°53' ecliptic, 6.5° equator.

sentences.zh: 三 曆官驗得太陰在赤道鬥宿十度，火星在赤道危宿六度強，土星在赤道虛宿六度半。

translations.literal: The three calendar officers verified the moon at equator Dipper ten degrees, Mars at equator Rooftop six degrees strong, Saturn at equator Emptiness six degrees half.
translations.idiomatic: Officers verified the moon at Dipper 10° equator, Mars at Rooftop 6°+ equator, Saturn at Emptiness 6.5° equator.

sentences.zh: 今考之太陰，《紀元曆》疏；

translations.literal: Examining now the moon, Jiyuan Calendar is sparse;
translations.idiomatic: For the moon, Jiyuan Calendar was loose;

sentences.zh: 火星，新曆、《紀元曆》全密，《統元曆》疏；

translations.literal: Mars—new calendar and Jiyuan Calendar fully dense, Unifying Origin Calendar sparse;
translations.idiomatic: Mars: new and Jiyuan calendars fully accurate, Unifying Origin loose;

sentences.zh: 土星，新曆全密，《紀元》、《統元曆》疏。」

translations.literal: Saturn—new calendar fully dense, Jiyuan and Unifying Origin calendars sparse."
translations.idiomatic: Saturn: new calendar fully accurate, Jiyuan and Unifying Origin loose."

sentences.zh: 又詔時與尚書禮部員外郎李燾同測驗，時等言：「先究《統元》、《紀元》、新曆異同，召三曆官上臺，用銅儀窺管對測太陰、土、火、木星晨度經歷度數，參稽所供，監視測驗。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Shi together with Ministry of Rites Outer Gentleman Li Tao to test; Shi and others said: "First investigate differences among Unifying Origin, Jiyuan, and new calendars, summon three calendar officers to the platform, use the bronze instrument sighting tube to measure moon, earth, fire, and wood stars' dawn degrees and traversed degrees, collate supplied materials and supervise tests.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered Shi and Li Tao of the Ministry of Rites to test jointly. They reported: first compare the three calendars, summon officers to the platform, and measure dawn positions of the moon and planets with the bronze armillary.

sentences.zh: 二十四日早晨度：《統元曆》太陰在黃道危宿十一度九十分，在赤道危宿九度；

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth morning degree: Unifying Origin Calendar moon on ecliptic Rooftop eleven degrees ninety parts, on equator Rooftop nine degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Morning of day 24 Unifying Origin: moon Rooftop 11°90' ecliptic, 9° equator;

sentences.zh: 木星在黃道室宿十八度一十五分，在赤道壁宿初度少；

translations.literal: wood star on ecliptic Encampments eighteen degrees fifteen parts, on equator Wall beginning little;
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter Encampments 18°15' ecliptic, Wall 0°− equator;

sentences.zh: 火星在黃道危宿十度七十分，在赤道危宿十度；

translations.literal: Mars on ecliptic Rooftop ten degrees seventy parts, on equator Rooftop ten degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Mars Rooftop 10°70' ecliptic, 10° equator;

sentences.zh: 土星在黃道虛宿八度九十五分，在赤道虛宿九度。

translations.literal: Saturn on ecliptic Emptiness eight degrees ninety-five parts, on equator Emptiness nine degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn Emptiness 8°95' ecliptic, 9° equator.

sentences.zh: 《紀元曆》太陰在赤道危宿十度五十三分，在赤道危宿八度半；

translations.literal: Jiyuan Calendar moon on equator Rooftop ten degrees fifty-three parts, on equator Rooftop eight degrees half;
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan: moon Rooftop 10°53' ecliptic, Rooftop 8.5° equator;

sentences.zh: 木星在黃道室宿十七度六十八分，在赤道室宿十四度少；

translations.literal: wood star on ecliptic Encampments seventeen degrees sixty-eight parts, on equator Encampments fourteen degrees little;
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter Encampments 17°68' ecliptic, 14°− equator;

sentences.zh: 火星在黃道危宿九度八十四分，在赤道危宿九度；

translations.idiomatic: Mars Rooftop 9°84' ecliptic, 9° equator;

sentences.zh: 土星在黃道留在虛宿七度四十分，在赤道虛宿七度半。

translations.literal: Saturn on ecliptic stationary at Emptiness seven degrees forty parts, on equator Emptiness seven degrees half.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn stationary at Emptiness 7°40' ecliptic, 7.5° equator.

sentences.zh: 新曆太陰在黃道危宿十三度五分，在赤道危宿十二度；

translations.literal: New calendar moon on ecliptic Rooftop thirteen degrees five parts, on equator Rooftop twelve degrees;
translations.idiomatic: New calendar: moon Rooftop 13°5' ecliptic, 12° equator;

sentences.zh: 木星在黃道室宿十八度一十分，在赤道室宿十六度半強；

translations.literal: wood star on ecliptic Encampments eighteen degrees ten parts, on equator Encampments sixteen degrees half strong;
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter Encampments 18°10' ecliptic, 16.5°+ equator;

sentences.zh: 火星在黃道危宿十度八分，在赤道危宿九度；

translations.literal: Mars on ecliptic Rooftop ten degrees eight parts, on equator Rooftop nine degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Mars Rooftop 10°8' ecliptic, 9° equator;

sentences.zh: 土星在黃道虛宿六度六十分始留，在赤道虛宿六度半強始留。

translations.literal: Saturn on ecliptic at Emptiness six degrees sixty parts beginning station, on equator Emptiness six degrees half strong beginning station.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn beginning station at Emptiness 6°60' ecliptic, 6.5°++ equator.

sentences.zh: 三曆官驗得太陰在赤道危宿十度，木星在赤道室宿十六度太，火星在赤道危宿九度半，土星在赤道虛宿六度半弱。

translations.literal: Three calendar officers verified moon at equator Rooftop ten degrees, wood star at equator Encampments sixteen degrees great, Mars at equator Rooftop nine degrees half, Saturn at equator Emptiness six degrees half weak.
translations.idiomatic: Officers verified moon Rooftop 10° equator, Jupiter Encampments 16°+ equator, Mars Rooftop 9.5° equator, Saturn Emptiness 6.5°− equator.

sentences.zh: 今考之太陰，《統元曆》精密、《紀元曆》、新曆皆疏；

translations.literal: Examining now the moon, Unifying Origin Calendar is precise and dense, Jiyuan Calendar and new calendar are all sparse;
translations.idiomatic: For the moon, Unifying Origin was precise; Jiyuan and the new calendar were loose;

sentences.zh: 木星，新曆稍密，《紀元》、《統元曆》皆疏；

translations.literal: wood star, new calendar slightly dense, Jiyuan and Unifying Origin calendars all sparse;
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter: new calendar slightly accurate; Jiyuan and Unifying Origin loose;

sentences.zh: 火星，《紀元》、新曆皆稍密，《統元曆》疏；

translations.literal: Mars, Jiyuan and new calendars both slightly dense, Unifying Origin Calendar sparse;
translations.idiomatic: Mars: Jiyuan and new slightly accurate; Unifying Origin loose;

sentences.zh: 土星，新曆稍密，《紀元》、《統元曆》皆疏。

translations.literal: Saturn, new calendar slightly dense, Jiyuan and Unifying Origin calendars all sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn: new slightly accurate; Jiyuan and Unifying Origin loose.

sentences.zh: 二十七日早晨度：《統元曆》木星在黃道壁宿初度四十六分，在赤道壁宿初度太強；

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh morning degree: Unifying Origin Calendar wood star on ecliptic Wall beginning forty-six parts, on equator Wall beginning great strong;
translations.idiomatic: Morning day 27 Unifying Origin: Jupiter Wall 0°46' ecliptic, 0°++ equator;

sentences.zh: 火星在黃道危宿十二度九十二分，在赤道危宿十二度強；

translations.literal: Mars on ecliptic Rooftop twelve degrees ninety-two parts, on equator Rooftop twelve degrees strong;
translations.idiomatic: Mars Rooftop 12°92' ecliptic, 12°+ equator;

sentences.zh: 土星留在黃道虛宿八度九十八分，在赤道虛宿九度。

translations.literal: Saturn stationary on ecliptic Emptiness eight degrees ninety-eight parts, on equator Emptiness nine degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn stationary Emptiness 8°98' ecliptic, 9° equator.

sentences.zh: 《紀元曆》木星在黃道壁宿初度二十五分，在赤道壁宿初度分空；

translations.literal: Jiyuan Calendar wood star on ecliptic Wall beginning twenty-five parts, on equator Wall beginning parts empty;
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan: Jupiter Wall 0°25' ecliptic, Wall 0° equator;

sentences.zh: 火星在黃道危宿十二度九十七分，在赤道危宿十一度；

translations.literal: Mars on ecliptic Rooftop twelve degrees ninety-seven parts, on equator Rooftop eleven degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Mars Rooftop 12°97' ecliptic, 11° equator;

translations.idiomatic: Saturn stationary Emptiness 7°48' ecliptic, 7.5° equator.

sentences.zh: 新曆木星在黃道壁宿初度四十四分，在赤道壁宿初少強；

translations.literal: New calendar wood star on ecliptic Wall beginning forty-four parts, on equator Wall beginning little strong;
translations.idiomatic: New calendar: Jupiter Wall 0°44' ecliptic, 0°−+ equator;

sentences.zh: 火星在黃道危宿十二度二十二分，在赤道危宿十一度半；

translations.literal: Mars on ecliptic Rooftop twelve degrees twenty-two parts, on equator Rooftop eleven degrees half;
translations.idiomatic: Mars Rooftop 12°22' ecliptic, 11.5° equator;

sentences.zh: 土星留在黃道虛宿六度六十分，在赤道虛宿六度半強。

translations.literal: Saturn stationary on ecliptic Emptiness six degrees sixty parts, on equator Emptiness six degrees half strong.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn stationary Emptiness 6°60' ecliptic, 6.5°+ equator.

sentences.zh: 三曆官驗得木星在赤道壁宿初度少，火星在赤道危宿十一度，土星在赤道虛宿六度半。

translations.literal: Three calendar officers verified wood star at equator Wall beginning little, Mars at equator Rooftop eleven degrees, Saturn at equator Emptiness six degrees half.
translations.idiomatic: Officers verified Jupiter Wall 0°− equator, Mars Rooftop 11° equator, Saturn Emptiness 6.5° equator.

sentences.zh: 今觀木星，新曆稍密，《紀元》、《統元曆》皆疏；

translations.literal: Examining now wood star, new calendar slightly dense, Jiyuan and Unifying Origin calendars all sparse;
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter: new slightly accurate; Jiyuan and Unifying Origin loose;

sentences.zh: 火星，《紀元曆》全密，《統元》、新曆皆疏；

translations.literal: Mars, Jiyuan Calendar fully dense, Unifying Origin and new calendars all sparse;
translations.idiomatic: Mars: Jiyuan fully accurate; Unifying Origin and new loose;

sentences.zh: 土星，新曆稍密，《紀元》、《統元曆》皆疏。」

sentences.zh: 由是朝廷始知三曆異同，乃詔太史局以新舊曆參照行之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the court first knew the three calendars' differences and similarities, and issued an edict the Astrological Bureau to implement by cross-referencing old and new calendars.
translations.idiomatic: The court thus learned how the three calendars differed and ordered the Astrological Bureau to implement them by cross-reference.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「新舊曆官互相異同，參照實難，新曆比之舊曆稍密。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "New and old calendar officers mutually differ; cross-referencing is truly difficult; the new calendar compared with old calendars is slightly dense."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites reported that new and old officers disagreed, making cross-reference difficult, though the new calendar was slightly more accurate.

sentences.zh: 詔用新曆，名以《乾道曆》，己丑歲頒行。

translations.literal: An edict adopted the new calendar, named Qiandao Calendar, promulgated in the jichou year.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted the new calendar, named the Qiandao Calendar, promulgated in the jichou year.

sentences.zh: 孝榮有《考春秋日食》一卷，《漢魏周隋日月交食》一卷，《唐日月交食》一卷，《宋朝日月交食》一卷，《氣朔入行》一卷，《強弱日法格數》一卷。

translations.literal: Xiaorong had one volume Investigating Spring and Autumn Solar Eclipses, one volume Han, Wei, Zhou, Sui Sun and Moon Eclipses, one volume Tang Sun and Moon Eclipses, one volume Song Dynasty Sun and Moon Eclipses, one volume Qi, New Moon, and Planetary Entry, one volume Strong and Weak Day Methods and Grid Numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaorong also authored Investigating Spring and Autumn Solar Eclipses, Han through Sui Eclipses, Tang Eclipses, Song Eclipses, Qi and New Moon Entry, and Strong-Weak Day Methods and Grid Numbers—one volume each.
